Keep the failed rubric criterion explicit.\nUse the existing category supported by the actual finding. The modern floor categories are\n`motion`, `surface_finish`, `pacing` and `ending_artistry`; source and integrity findings keep\ntheir existing categories. Do not return these findings only as strings or bury them in notes.\nEach A/B code report must stand alone inside a combined handoff, with its original assessment\nand exact bindings. Optional preferences remain notes, never invented mandatory categories.\n\n## What you are looking for\n\n**Genuine divergence, not a relabel.** Two scenes that both say \"wide establishing shot\" with\ndifferent nouns are one scene twice. Composition, camera move, scale and subject must actually\ndiffer.\n\n**Film-level construction.** Count `visual_family` and `payload_mode`, not just scene signatures.\nTwo families carrying most of the runtime or a sequence of figures delivered as text panels is a\nstructural ceiling. Props cannot repair it later.\n\n**The early payoff is a picture.** Read its deadline from `config/documentary.json`.\nScene one names a real strategy and visible payoff. An establishing shot, title, or promise\nthat something will become interesting later is not a hook.\n\n**Picture-led.** Follow the action with the narration and labels covered. If the story\nonly works with narration, it is a podcast with pictures and it fails here.\n\n**Input is not processing proof.** If narration describes scanning, analyzing, selecting or another transformation, a captured input image alone does not prove that action. The current phone film must show the transformation and a completed visible consequence in the same objects. Captions may explain scope; they cannot supply a missing action. A retained still can be valid evidence, but an unchanged inset is not an analysis beat. Compare the native rejection interval with the new phone pixels before approving the same mechanism again.\n\n**Judge the dominant picture, not peripheral motion.** A small moving sliver behind a large static inset does not repair the inset's pacing. Inspect the actual native hero at phone size and native crop scale: recognizable silhouettes at 270 pixels can conceal unfinished surfaces, faceted props and missing contact shadows. Compare all unresolved native defects together before the next render; do not approve a label, outline or tiny prop change as a complete repair. If the same dominant layout has failed twice, require a changed composition or action mechanism before another native attempt.\n\n**Sentence-to-pixel proof.** Ignore `on_screen`, `what_moves` and `hero` on the first pass. For\neach VO line, inspect `visual_proof.must_show`, resolve every `item_id` into `planes[].items`, and\nask whether those actual components and props make the sentence literal. A generic pickup under a\nreadout is not a model joining records. If the binding is technically present but visually tiny\nor dominated by unrelated context, revise it.\n\n**Docket flow.** The scene roles should cause one another: movement, consequence, honest limit,\nthen agency. A list of facts can be accurate and still have no story. The close should answer\n\"what happens next\" rather than merely restate the hook.\n\n**Attention earns each interval.** Read `config/documentary.json` and the craft guide. Resolve\n`attention_beats` through the scene event ids, including the gap to the ending. The hook must\nactually pay off within the policy window. A line of text, a camera drift or an animated dash\ncannot rescue a subject that does nothing. The faster direction asks for action, consequence,\nevidence or human response while preserving time to understand each idea.\n\n**Motivated framing.** The camera can hold while a subject acts or evidence is read. Move it to\nreveal a relationship, follow an action or change the viewer's understanding. Do not add orbiting\nor zooming merely to advertise the engine. A continuous action may span multiple scene records.\n\n**Three images before a finished film.** Identify the opening payoff, central mechanism and\nclosing consequence. Ask which image will be remembered and what question it resolves. If these\nare three cards with labels, reboard before spending a render. Check the actual source of every\nreconstruction and whether its visual certainty exceeds the reporting.\n\n**Visual access before visual promises.** For each of those three images, name the public\nreference or source fact that permits its depiction. If the pivotal action occurs inside a\nprivate interface, lab or workplace that no source shows, do not approve a sequence of invented\nscreens and pointing gestures as observed workflow. Require an explicitly illustrated mechanism\nwhose state visibly changes, or send the director back to a more filmable source-backed angle.\nAn event list with verbs is insufficient when the same generic panel remains the dominant image.\n\n**Region correctness.** The scene's region comes from the story's county. A board that puts a Hill\nCountry palette on a Panhandle story is wrong before it is drawn.\n\nReturn the complete bound gate-ready report described above. The fields `verdict`, `notes`,\n`strongest_frame` and `weakest_frame` are part of that report, not a substitute for its bindings,\n`story_review`, action reviews or the timed phone and modern observations required at phone scope.\n\n`weakest_frame` is required. Every board has one and naming it is more useful than praise.\n\n\nApply the dated policy: config/cinematic_production.json through September 28 and\nconfig/creative_production.json afterward. Reject a missing cinema plan, decorative pictures\nor a hero passage that cannot be understood at phone size. The new policy has no 3D quota.\nRead CREATIVE_DIRECTION.md, resolve source picture ids into actual native assets, and inspect\nsource fidelity, relevant detail, whole-sequence continuity and the answered opening question.\nFor the initial code assignment review both opening boards in one reserved task. For the\ninitial phone assignment compare the two actual preview openings and review the chosen whole\nsequence, returning the bound selection and ordinary exact-phone verdict. Do not add a third\noption, another judge, or an extra paid review for a preference.\nRequire a real customer or human action where the story claims one. Review the finished hero\nproof before the full cut. A camera move, texture change or tiny hand gesture is not sufficient.\n\n**A person must perform the claimed action.** A generated presenter cutout sliding, fading, or\ncrossfading between poses does not establish a handoff. Inspect where the object starts, what\nmoves it, where it lands, and what changes afterward. Reject disconnected hands, duplicate props,\nunmotivated disappearance, or an idle figure held through the opening. If the medium cannot\nperform the action credibly, redesign the shot before granting a code-plan pass.\n\nFollow the complete visible shoulder, upper arm, elbow, forearm and hand through the action. Clear contact-point rays do not prove that the limb avoids the prop: an opaque clipboard can hide an intersecting upper arm and leave a detached-looking forearm. Check the full occupied volumes and then the actual phone pixels. Actor orientation must support the action: an inspector examining a house must visibly attend to the house or its image, rather than face the audience while pointing behind the body. Grounded weight shifts need planted feet and articulated hips or knees; rotating an entire rigid figure is not a performed stance change.\n\nCheck physical scale before contact detail: compare the person's height with the door, window,\ntools and carried object, and verify a shared ground. Sample upper-arm and forearm lengths\nthrough the complete performance. Arbitrary curved tubes, stretched reach and silent target\nclamping can preserve contact while breaking believable motion. A supported prop or clear\nsilhouette alone cannot clear those defects. Inspect actual native surface and motion quality\nafter the phone pass; keep those two review scopes explicit.\n\n**Review the occupied picture space.** Check the principal subject at the beginning, contact,\nand result of each event against the actual shared caption band and title overlays. Inspect\nphone frames at all three moments, not only a representative contact-sheet frame. A moving\nobject whose landing is hidden by captions fails even if its path is visible. The ending of an\naction must remain readable long enough to explain the next shot.\n\nFor editions dated September 26 onward, inspect the exact phone MP4 before reading the\ndirector's explanation. Record phone_observations with subject_recognition,\ncontact_and_consequence, surface_finish, and closing_payoff. Each contains pass,\nstart_s, end_s and observed: describe the actual pixels and the specific action.\nReject placeholder boxes standing in for recognizable machinery or homes, ambiguous\nprops, floating transfers, rigid cleanup gestures, and an ending that repeats setup.\nDo not infer a resolved human outcome when the sources leave it unknown. Judge the\nsource-backed limit as an image with a visible consequence. A code-plan pass cannot\npopulate these observations; only the current rendered phone film can.\n\n\n## Shared quality standard\n\nFor current art-profile packets, read ART_DIRECTION.md and the frozen cinematic reference\nbank in full. Existing source, rights, action, native, audio, captions,\ncumulative resources, finite artistic recovery and shipment requirements continue.\n\n## Director\n\nBefore coding, choose the visual approach from actual source access. Think through four\nlenses in the existing director assignment: the comedian finds an observable mismatch;\nthe dramatist finds pressure and a changed state; the explainer finds the causal relation;\nthe enthusiast finds a specific surprising detail. Explain seven palette\nroles, contrasting shapes, the recognizable hero silhouette and its finish, motivated\nlight, focal hierarchy, action timing, and one signature shot tied to an actual event.\nName the current asset and actual subject ids. For the illustrated carton route, use `flat_shots`\nwith native-coordinate offsets, scale and a reason. Numeric shot choices must be executed\nby the routed scene, not left as board prose. A custom renderer must consume the same\nprofile or explain its retained source lighting and implement its relevant choices.\n\nThe focal object stays sharp. Depth blur must arise from actual separation and preserve\ncontact detail. Never add blur, floating shapes, lens flares, camera kicks or orbiting as\nautomatic cinematic decoration. Hold the camera while an object performs. Move it to reveal\na relation or follow a finite action. Give a completed result a comprehension hold.\n\n## Scene builder and render owner\n\nUse `prompts/roles/scene-builder.md` in the existing code assignment. Build the finished\nhero first, then light and stage it before extending the scene. Recognizable geometry,\nedges, seams, hardware, texture and grounded shadows beat a field of placeholder primitives.\nAuthored 2.5D, useful footage and a readable source image can outperform complicated 3D.\nDo not restrict the daily story to the demonstration subject or copy reference b-roll.\n\nThe shared `ArtDirectionProvider` carries current choices in both entry points. Three.js\n`CinematicStage`/`Studio` execute the light recipe and exposure. `directedShot` executes\nauthored event-bound cameras. The illustrated carton component executes its flat framing,\nfinished surfaces, occlusion and contact assemblies. Source footage retains original speed\nand practical lighting. Existing boards without this profile retain their original defaults.\n\nEvery new event specifies a motion curve within its existing measured window: `travel`\naccelerates and brakes; `contact` approaches and settles; `linear` serves constant-speed\nmovement; `smoothstep` is available for a justified gentle transition. `anticipation` and\n`settle` reserve fractions inside that window, never new runtime or voice stretching.\n`landing` has a small overshoot and needs a free-prop reason; never use it for a constrained\ncontact, a foot planted on ground, or a source-implied machine limit. Check music and foley\nagainst the executed contact, not the old curve. No incidental sway substitutes for action.\n\nJudge motion at the delivered 30 fps. This is one shared engineering advance, not five new stylistic attempts.\nFund the entire remaining production/review/delivery path before changing the renderer.\nDo not delay an accepted cut for optional engineering or add roles, reviews or resource grants.\n","knowledge/craft/AUTHORED_STORY_ART.md":"# Fresh authored story pictures\n\nThe owner selected this Claude substitute on October 9th, 2026. Keep camera movement motivated and finite; do not copy every decorative effect from a stronger reference.\"\n  }\n}\n","knowledge/craft/visual-storytelling/README.md":"# Visual storytelling for Dispatch\n\nResearch and direction revision: October 2nd, 2026.\n\nThe picture, narration and captions must describe the same unfolding story. The picture supplies a recognizable subject, relationship, action or consequence. Narration explains its significance and limits. Captions give access to the spoken account. A moving object is useful only when the viewer understands what it represents and what its change means.\n\nThese dossiers combine researched craft with proposed Dispatch practice. Source observations are identified and linked. The shot methods, selection procedure and worked example are our production recommendations, not claims that research guarantees audience engagement.\n\n## Choose the story's visual approach\n\nRead this index and the chosen dossier in full before boarding. Select by the available evidence and the explanation the viewer needs. Keep one primary approach; supporting footage or documents should connect to that approach through a clear subject or question.\n\n| Approach | Choose when | What it must show | Reject when |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| [Observed documentary](observed-documentary.md) | Authenticated footage shows the actual people, place, equipment or workflow | A real action and its observed result | Similar-looking stock replaces the story's actual identity |\n| [Explanatory animation](explanatory-animation.md) | The central process or comparison is hard to see directly | Recognizable input, meaningful transformation and readable output | Abstract objects require a private legend to decode |\n| [Evidence-led imagery](evidence-led-imagery.md) | Relevant photographs or documents carry the reporting | What the evidence establishes and how it changes the answer | A sequence of screenshots substitutes for the entire mechanism |\n| [Cinematic scene](cinematic-scene.md) | A source-backed physical task, obstacle and consequence can sustain a scene | Spatially coherent action, a turn and a consequential ending | Lighting, orbiting props or music replace story development |\n\nUse this selection order:\n\n1. State the viewer's question, sourced action, affected person or group and honest ending.\n2. Inventory inspected, usable assets and demonstrated components. Record what each can and can't show.\n3. Choose the approach that makes the central relationship easiest to understand. Explain the rejected alternative in one sentence.\n4. Complete the [sentence-to-shot worksheet](sentence-to-shot.md). Resolve missing pictures before locking narration.\n5. Compare exactly two genuinely different complete treatments in the existing shared preview batch. Read the selected dossier for each treatment. Preserve the current contracts, frozen budget and existing independent roles.\n6. Have the existing critic inspect the actual rendered sequence before reading the director's explanation. A filled worksheet does not prove comprehension.\n\nDo not impose a weekday rotation. Track the selected approach in the existing creative-direction rationale so the director can see recent repetition. When two approaches fit equally well, variety can break the tie. Never choose variety at the expense of truth or comprehension.\n\n## Choose a format and think through its sequence\n\nFor newly planned editions from October 3rd, read the [viewer planning method](viewer-plan.md) in full. Distinguish the format from the medium: a news report can use observed footage, illustration or documents; an educational explainer can return from a diagram to physical evidence; a cinematic scene still needs a truthful task and consequence.\n\nFor a news report read [the reporting dossier](news-reporting.md) and choose its human-led, mechanism-led or evidence-led structure from the actual story. Record why the order works, the likely false inference and the carried subject across each cut in the existing creative-direction and transition fields. The [national-news study](broadcast-cadence-study.md) identifies the observed examples and access limits. It does not prescribe a single bracketed rundown.\n\nThe director and workers use these short decision reasons to choose and challenge the treatment. A copied structure, named style or completed worksheet supplies no quality verdict. The packet tools bind the current method and relevant approach text; remote recovery supplies the actual text because a provider can't open local links.\n\n## Give the three channels distinct jobs\n\n**See:** Show the thing being discussed at the moment it is discussed. Preserve its identity across the cut. Make any comparison legible before asking the viewer to infer a result.\n\n**Hear:** Name the relationship, cause or uncertainty that the picture can't establish alone. Time emphasis and event sound to the actual reveal. A music swell can't supply an unreported outcome.\n\n**Read:** Retain complete measured captions. Use brief object labels only where they identify a picture or distinction. Avoid simultaneous paragraph copy competing with both the action and captions. Lay out the decisive result above the real caption band and hold it long enough to understand.\n\nMayer's research summary supports removing distracting content, placing related words near pictures and presenting corresponding animation and narration together. It also reports redundancy effects in multimedia learning. These are learning findings, not a forecast of short-video retention; they do not justify removing accessible captions. Our application is to reduce competing editorial text while maintaining captions. [Cambridge multimedia-learning chapter](https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/abs/cambridge-handbook-of-multimedia-learning/principles-for-reducing-extraneous-processing-in-multimedia-learning-coherence-signaling-redundancy-spatial-contiguity-and-temporal-contiguity-principles/C98AB3A6CE760DD63C048936EA0B3B44), [W3C caption guidance](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/captions-prerecorded).\n\n## Review what the viewer receives\n\nUse the existing review assignments and fixed rubric. Add these observations to their existing consolidated notes, not a new scorecard or paid role.\n\n- **Recognition:** Before reading the board, what does the principal object look like? Can the critic name it without guessing?\n- **Alignment:** At each narrated clause, does the picture show the named subject and relationship? Record exact film times for contradictions or absent concepts.\n- **Development:** What changed, and how does that change lead to the next shot? Distinguish subject transformation from decorative motion.\n- **Continuity:** Is the same person, site, sample or document being followed? Is a different example disclosed?\n- **Combined comprehension:** After one viewing with audio and captions, what happened, who can act and what remains unproven?\n- **Picture contribution:** With narration muted and captions covered, which parts of the central process can the viewer actually see? Dates and attribution may rely on text; the principal action can't.\n- **Ending:** Does the final picture answer the opening question without inventing implementation, savings, approval or repair?\n\nAn unrecognizable object, absent principal action or contradictory picture is a comprehension/source defect under the current contract. Do not classify it as merely style because pixels move. Surface polish and optional camera preferences remain artistic issues. Retain all real rejected verdicts and use the existing repair and bounded-release policies.\n\n## Apply this without expanding production\n\nUse the current budget precheck for the complete review and render path before spending. Keep the bounded visual search, source and rights evidence, prior-edition identity gate, two-treatment comparison, native hero, phone inspection, audiovisual lenses and independent scorers. The dossiers introduce no render quota, new reviewer or budget extension.\n\nRead [the October 2nd diagnosis and proposed sequence](october-2-pavement-case.md) for the difference between a source-related object and a picture that communicates the spoken claim.\n\n## Research status\n\nSources were accessed October 2nd, 2026. The four approach dossiers use published guidance, research summaries and practitioner accounts; their linked film examples are references rather than claimed viewing. The separate national-news study adds explicitly scoped transcripts and rendered samples. Today's diagnosis uses the listed native frame samples and retained board; it is not a replacement independent whole-film review. Research access does not grant reuse rights to any publisher's images, footage or soundtrack.\n","knowledge/craft/visual-storytelling/evidence-led-imagery.md":"# Evidence-led imagery\n\nRead the [shared visual-storytelling direction](README.md) first.\n\n## What this approach does\n\nIt lets the viewer examine real reporting evidence: a site photograph, source image, dated document, map or published result. It is useful when authentic footage is unavailable and the evidence has concrete visual content.\n\nChoose it when the viewer's question concerns what a document establishes, where a change occurs, who is involved or what a photographed condition actually looks like. It can support an explanatory sequence; it must not turn an entire process story into reading screenshots.\n\n## Research findings and limits\n\nNPR Visuals describes sequential stories combining photography and text, sometimes with audio, video or illustration. Its retrospective reports varied completion performance and cautions that strong visuals and the story itself are essential. Those observations concern interactive web stories and do not establish short-video performance. [NPR's sequential-story analysis](https://blog.apps.npr.org/2015/11/19/sequential-visual-stories.html).\n\nReuters' standards require accurate images and attribution that identifies outside material's actual source. They prohibit fabrication and warn against visual changes that misrepresent reality. This supports honest identity and presentation; it does not grant licences for Reuters or other publishers' media. [Reuters standards](https://reutersagency.com/about/standards-values/).\n\n## Dispatch method\n\nGive every asset a specific evidentiary job. Before boarding, record the claim it supports, the detail the viewer will inspect, what lies outside its evidentiary scope, and its established reuse rights. A portrait identifies a person. A site image establishes visible conditions at its documented place and time. Neither proves an unseen workflow.\n\nArrange the evidence around a question:\n\n| Stage | Picture function | Editing choice |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Orient | Show the actual site, subject or full source context | Hold a readable establishing view |\n| Inspect | Reveal the one detail that supports the claim | A purposeful crop or highlight |\n| Compare | Show a documented contrast, location or relationship | Matched views with honest identities |\n| Establish scope | Identify date, issuer and limitation | A brief readable source passage |\n| Return | Connect the evidence to the physical consequence | Return to the subject, changed understanding |\n\nEach cut should answer the previous shot's question. Do not count a new excerpt, title or fade as a new development when it repeats the same information.\n\nFor a document, show enough context to establish its identity, then expose the decisive passage. Preserve surrounding qualifications that change the claim. An enlarged crop must not make a planned feature look delivered. Use an original explanatory panel when a truthful transcription is clearer, and disclose it; do not fabricate a screenshot.\n\nFor a photograph, keep the actual detail visible. Camera movement should reveal geography, scale or a relationship, not simply animate an inert image. Do not use a crop to imply a different place or eliminate context that changes interpretation. Do not animate a real still into an invented observed event.\n\n## Pair evidence with explanation\n\nIf the story says a system processes data, a screenshot of its input supports the input claim only. To explain the transformation, pair it with a disclosed source-bound animation or authenticated output. Do not fill the rest of the film with underlines and excerpts because a source page is easy to obtain.\n\nFor the pavement story, a verified example of surface and range imagery could support a comparison. A university article supports attribution and date. It does not supply proof of a completed road repair. When usable technical images have no established rights, draw an explicitly conceptual explanation instead.\n\nKeep complete captions in their measured band. A dense passage and a long spoken sentence can overload the phone frame; use only the necessary excerpt and preserve its source context in the existing evidence package. Narration should explain the visible detail rather than read an unrelated paragraph over it.\n\n## Before voice and final review\n\nThe existing critic should explain what each asset proves and where the sequence implies more. Ask whether the film still has a principal action and consequence under the current contract. Reject the known whole-film screenshot-and-fading-box approach before spending.\n\nKeep the prior-edition identity check, native asset provenance, rights evidence and normal phone review. If no useful external imagery is available, omit the insert and move on. The fallback must remain a complete explanatory treatment, not a stalled stock search.\n","knowledge/craft/visual-storytelling/news-reporting.md":"# Direct a coherent news report\n\nThe [cadence study](broadcast-cadence-study.md) records the evidence behind this dossier. The structures below are Dispatch production choices, not a universal network script. Apply them to newly planned editions from October 3rd, 2026; preserve shipped editions and their real reviews.\n\nA report has an editorial spine: a specific situation, a question, evidence that changes the answer, an explanation, an honest consequence and a close. Decide which of those jobs the next shot performs. A source-related image that supplies no new understanding is a weak insert, even if its colors and motion look expensive.\n\n## Choose the order from the story\n\n| Reporting structure | Choose it when | Sequence of reporting jobs | Ending test |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| Human-led report | The evidence identifies a real person's task, obstacle or changed options | Show the task or consequence \u2192 establish the dated change \u2192 broaden with evidence \u2192 explain the cause and limits \u2192 return to the same person or task | Has the viewer learned what changes for that person, without an invented reaction or outcome? |\n| Mechanism-led report | The central news is a process, measurement or decision that viewers can't readily see | Show a recognizable input and question \u2192 orient the source and setting \u2192 reveal the transformation \u2192 show the result \u2192 connect it to a human decision and its limits | Can the viewer explain the input, transformation and result, and distinguish an illustration from observed operation? |\n| Evidence-led report | A filing, policy, measurement or public record changes the reported answer | Establish the dated decision or disputed claim \u2192 expose the decisive source detail \u2192 explain its effect with a concrete relationship \u2192 show affected options or activity \u2192 state the unresolved point and next decision | Does the ending answer what the record establishes, who can act next and what it does not establish? |\n\nChoose one structure. Compress or reorder it when the evidence and viewer's question justify that choice. Establish the essential source limitation when the affected claim appears; a later caveat can't undo a misleading picture. Keep the current early-picture payoff and event timing requirements. These sequences introduce no extra scenes, prescribed shot seconds or runtime quota.\n\nThe CBS transcript in the study provides a specific-to-broad-to-specific example. The CNN transcript shows a different package organization, and the MSNBC example is a question-led interview. They are different forms with different access to people and evidence. A short Dispatch should not imitate a lengthy panel simply because it resembles national television.\n\n## Assign each ingredient a reporting job\n\n**Opening:** Give the viewer something identifiable to understand immediately: a task interrupted, an input changing, a decision confronting evidence, or a completed consequence that creates a question. State the actual question soon enough to guide the picture. A dramatic claim must stay within the fetched evidence. Do not borrow an unrelated victim, emergency or reaction to manufacture stakes.\n\n**Orientation:** Establish who, where and what changed using the minimum needed narration and labels. This is the short-video equivalent of the paragraph that explains the focus of an article. The viewer should know why the next piece of evidence belongs in this story.\n\n**Reporter or presenter:** Use an actual reusable field passage when it demonstrates, verifies or bridges the explanation. A fabricated journalist, microphone prop or studio cut adds no verification. Dispatch's narrator can orient the viewer without appearing as a reporter. A person on screen must have a source-backed role and perform an understandable action.\n\n**Evidence:** Show the exact place, equipment, task, relevant photograph or decisive source words. Identify what the evidence establishes. A quotation is evidence of what its speaker said; it is not proof that their conclusion is true. Show a contrary finding or uncertainty when the story requires it. Use the existing source and rights lanes for every asset.\n\n**Explanation:** Introduce coded visuals when they reveal a relationship that the authentic image can't show. Keep the same physical subject or explicitly identify the new example. The diagram should answer the question created by the preceding shot. Return to the source image or human decision after the explanation when that return completes the thought.\n\n**Consequence and close:** Show how the action changes a state, choice, risk or next step. Answer the opening question through the completed visible action. Distinguish a demonstrated consequence, an expected effect and an unknown eventual outcome. Do not repeat the introduction merely to make the film seem circular. A return earns its place when the viewer now understands the original subject differently.\n\n## Move between authentic pictures and coded explanation\n\nMake each handoff explicit in the existing edit notes. Carry a stable identifying detail: the same road patch, sample, site, device, document passage or clearly disclosed example. Preserve orientation, useful scale and the relationship under explanation. An outline or highlight identifies a region; it does not prove that a machine detected, measured or classified it.\n\nFor example, an authenticated image can establish the input. An explicitly illustrated transformation can explain the source-supported relationship. A return to the actual task can show who uses the result. Cutting from an unrelated office image to anonymous blocks and then to a different city breaks that connection, even if every image is broadly about AI.\n\nOriginal illustration is a valid principal medium. Useful footage is also valid. An irrelevant insert should be omitted within the existing bounded search. Do not commission an unproven rig or prolong the stock hunt to imitate a particular outlet. Use the current source-backed action admission when a genuinely necessary mechanism needs implementation.\n\n## Direct the cadence across picture, voice and reading\n\nGive each beat one new idea the viewer needs for the next beat. Complete its decisive event before cutting. Preserve enough time to recognize the subject, follow the change and read the result. Trim repeated setup before requesting faster narration. Pace varies with information and action; a cut on a fixed timer is not an editorial reason.\n\nVoice should orient, reveal, explain, qualify or resolve. Tell the VO director which job a line performs and where the visual answer lands. Keep the approved continuous script and measured alignment. Use contrast in intent and emphasis rather than perpetual urgency. Do not turn a hypothesis into certainty through a triumphant delivery or sound cue.\n\nNatural sound, verified interview audio and motivated effects can connect thoughts when their provenance and actual event timing support that use. A sound bridge can carry the same action over a cut. Sound can't imply recorded access to a site we did not visit. Preserve intelligibility and all existing audio checks.\n\nRetain complete captions. Keep extra labels short and attached to the object they identify. Do not present a second paragraph, a busy diagram and a new location at the same time as a dense spoken sentence. Seeing, hearing and reading should reinforce the same unfolding account.\n\n## Review the actual report\n\nThe existing critic and scorers reconstruct the story from the current film before consulting the director's rationale. They identify what the opening asks, what new information arrives in the middle, how subject identity survives each handoff, and what the ending answers. Then they compare that understanding with the approved words and fetched evidence.\n\nUse exact intervals and the existing observation fields. A missing principal action, unrecognizable subject, false visual implication or failed explanation remains a source/comprehension failure under the current contract. Optional presenter preferences, shot polish and an alternative ordering alone do not create a new mandatory test. Keep the fixed rubric and retain every actual rejection.\n","knowledge/craft/visual-storytelling/viewer-plan.md":"# Make the editorial choice before the picture\n\nApply this method to newly planned editions from October 3rd, 2026. It guides decisions under the current contracts and does not certify quality. It adds no board schema, scorer, research pass or paid attempt.\n\n## Decide and record\n\nRead the selector and chosen approach dossier in full. For a news report also read the reporting dossier. Use the existing creative_direction and story_contract fields; keep the decision rationale compact and inspectable.\n\n1. **Focus.** In viewer_question and visible_answer, state what changes, for whom, through which sourced action. Name the expected viewer takeaway and the strongest honest limit. Distinguish the narrative answer from an unknown eventual outcome.\n2. **Choose.** Begin medium_choice with the named format and approach: News report, Educational explainer or Cinematic scene; then Observed documentary, Explanatory animation, Evidence-led imagery or Cinematic scene. Explain why the available assets can carry the explanation and why a plausible alternative is weaker. Naming an approach is a routing aid, not an approval field.\n3. **Order.** Put each beat's reporting job in the existing scene advances and edit notes. For a report choose human-led, mechanism-led or evidence-led ordering. Explain why this evidence appears here and what question it creates or answers. Educational explanation builds a recognizable example through successive states. A cinematic scene follows a task, obstacle, consequential turn and completed action. Do not apply one rundown to all three.\n4. **Anticipate confusion.** Name the most likely false inference and the picture or immediate source limit that prevents it. In emotional_turn, connect the viewer's changing understanding to an evidenced stake. Do not invent a person's feelings or claim to know the audience's reaction.\n5. **Connect.** In enter_on, leave_on, cut_after_event_id and next_connection, name the visible event, new information and carried subject. Complete the event before the cut. A footage-to-diagram handoff keeps the same identified example or discloses a new one. Finish the sentence-to-shot worksheet inside these existing notes.\n6. **Direct and test.** Tie line intent, emphasis, motivated sound and captions to the actual reveal. Before spending, ask what remains understandable with narration muted and editorial labels covered, then test the combined account. Essential dates and attribution can use text; the principal action must read in the picture. Budget the entire remaining review/render path, including independent-provider recovery where required.\n\nThese are short decision reasons a colleague can inspect, not a request for a private stream of thought. Use concrete evidence and an alternative that could realistically be built. Do not fill every field with the same sentence, duplicate the research or commission a third treatment.\n\n## Each worker has a distinct decision\n\n- **Researcher:** Identify the most informative picture and the strongest limitation. Recommend an angle that the assets can actually show; flag the sentence for which no truthful picture exists.\n- **Director:** Choose the story focus, format, medium and order. Resolve the weak handoff before narration, using the same two-treatment batch and consolidated ledger.\n- **VO director:** Translate the approved beat jobs into a continuous performance. Explain a lift, drop or pause through the reveal it supports; preserve the words and alignment.\n- **Code critic:** Determine whether the proposed implementation can perform the action and carry the explanation. A planned gesture is not a watched result.\n- **Phone critic and scorers:** First describe what is recognizable and what changes in the actual film. Then compare with the approved account. Locate the weakest identity or information handoff and classify the observed defect under the existing criteria. Keep their separate assigned lenses and actual verdicts.\n\nFor remote independent recovery, the supplied packet contains the actual method, selector, reporting dossier and named approach text. If a director has not named an approach, all four approach guides are supplied rather than pretending an unread local path was available. The new teaching bundle is added only for editions from October 3rd. A text packet never establishes audiovisual access.\n\n## Why the handoff needs thought\n\nAn original film-comprehension study associated event boundaries with meaningful changes in characters, objects, place, goals and causes. Our application is to preserve those relationships across a cut and make a change understandable. This is an editorial inference, not a scientifically established short-video pacing interval or retention guarantee. [Zacks and colleagues, The Brain's Cutting-Room Floor](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/human-neuroscience/articles/10.3389/fnhum.2010.00168/full).\n\nThe director can consult the [observed news examples](broadcast-cadence-study.md) when a reporting choice needs a model. Workers use the supplied method, relevant guide and current artifacts without repeatedly reloading the research corpus. scenes.vo: Anyone in San Antonio can now hail a Waymo with no driver, the airport included.

The phone ride request pin slides to the curb and changes to arriving as the car settles at the bay mark.

requests.purpose: Give the film one generic white driverless car design that performs five different sourced examples, each disclosed on screen as its own illustration: an airport arrival with an empty steering wheel, an empty car carried off in a creek, another empty car stopped in floodwater, a car slowing into standing water as the recall sentence words it, and a generic airport ride waiting at the curb. Within each example every state the car reaches is kept for that scene.
requests.prompt: Author an original finished React and SVG object in the current Remotion engine. A long rounded white sport utility robotaxi with a roof sensor pod, small side sensors, dark glass that shows an empty driver seat and a steering wheel, black wheel arches, visible rims, lit headlamps, brake lamps and amber hazard lamps, a scuffed lower door, a mud line that rises after water, and a rear door that opens. Late sodium light from the upper left, cool fill from the right, a long soft shadow. No logos, no brand marks and no real model badge. Maintained but worn, nothing symmetric. A disclosed illustration, never a real vehicle.
requests.source_limit: Disclosed illustration of a generic white driverless car. Not a Waymo vehicle, a vehicle in the recall, a real road, speed, depth or rider.

story_contract.opening_question: Anyone in San Antonio can now hail a driverless Waymo to the airport. What does the federal record say about the flood problem its recall covers?
story_contract.actor: Waymo, with a recall record held by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration
story_contract.action: Opened its San Antonio robotaxi rides to anyone with the app, airport included, after filing a software recall about driving into standing water.
story_contract.change: Driverless rides in San Antonio move from invited riders in a limited area to anyone with the app, while the recall remedy is still listed as under development.
story_contract.affected_people: People who can now hail a ride, airport travelers among them. The April cars were empty and no one was injured, and no rider is named.
story_contract.consequence: A federal record that still lists the flood remedy as under development, beside an interim step of tighter weather limits by April 20th.
story_contract.source_limit: The recall wording is one sentence with no cause, speed or depth. The record does not say what the weather limits are or whether they apply now, and the recall notice itself was not retrieved.
story_contract.closing_answer: The airport ride is open, and the federal record still lists the flood remedy as under development.

captions.text: Anyone in San Antonio can now hail a Waymo with no driver,
in a limited area of sixty square miles.
In April, an empty Waymo was swept into Salado Creek.
Earlier that month, another empty car was stranded in floodwater.
that could affect nearly thirty eight hundred cars.
The recall says the software may let a car slow,
then drive into standing water on higher speed roads.
The federal record says the remedy is currently under development.
As an interim step, Waymo tightened its weather limits,
and every affected car had the update by April twentieth.
So the airport ride is open,
and the federal record lists the flood remedy

files.config/dispatch_rubric.yaml:
# THE BAR LIVES HERE AND NOWHERE ELSE.
#
# Never restate this number in a prompt, a brief, or a verdict file. The sibling lost five panel
# rounds to exactly that: its routine prompt carried one number while this file carried another,
# so the panel was briefed the stale one and returned ship:false on a cut that was already over
# the real bar. Two judges flagged the divergence unprompted and the run kept grading against the
# wrong number anyway.
#
# A number restated in a second place is a number that will be wrong in one of them.
#
# AND THIS HEADER PROVED IT ON 2026-08-19. It used to tell that story by quoting both numbers,
# so the file whose whole job is to hold one bar carried two more in its own comment, four lines
# under the sentence forbidding it. The owner moved the bar that morning and all three judges of
# round 22 reported being briefed the old one; every one of them also flagged that a judge who
# skims this header before reaching the value below reads the stale figure as live. The numerals
# are gone. Anyone who needs the number reads the field.
#
# WHY THE BAR CAME DOWN OFF THE ORIGINAL. The sibling recalibrated with the reason written down:
# the original was implicitly calibrated against a painterly fidelity this brand deliberately
# does not use, so the ceiling on every run became the house style itself, and the panel's
# weakest axis was "the flat vector characters" for nine straight rounds while every concrete
# defect got fixed. A bar that can only be cleared by abandoning the house style is not a bar,
# it is a disagreement about the style, and it belongs in a style decision rather than a score.
rubric:
  # Set by the owner on 2026-08-19, down from where it had been.
  # This is the ONLY place the bar lives and the only place it may be changed.
  # A run does not get to move it: a below-bar final panel remains active repair,
  # and delivery requires the hash-bound passing report. Only verified shipment
  # completes a production run. The owner controls any change to this bar.
  ship_threshold: 7.0

  axes:
    hook:
      weight: 0.18
      asks: >
        Would a stranger stop scrolling in the first two seconds, with the sound off? The first
        frame is the whole decision. A title card is not a hook.
    story:
      weight: 0.20
      asks: >
        Does this feel like Texas AI Docket moving today: a dated actor, decision or application,
        consequence, honest limit, and what happens next? Is there an earned take rather than a
        summary, and does the piece turn somewhere the viewer did not see coming?
    picture:
      weight: 0.20
      asks: >
        Does every five seconds pay in motion, emotion or revelation? Is anything a held slide
        with a voice over it? With captions hidden, does each shot literally depict the sentence
        being spoken rather than reuse generic Texas scenery?
    place:
      weight: 0.14
      asks: >
        Would a Texan from that county believe the person who drew this had been there? Region
        light, vegetation, kit and cast all correct for the story's actual county.
    craft:
      weight: 0.14
      asks: >
        Camera movement motivated by the action; deliberate holds when the subject acts or evidence
        is read. Depth and sound clarify cause and consequence. Type legible at feed size. Nothing
        symmetric that should not be. Maintained but worn, not new and not ruined.
    voice:
      weight: 0.14
      asks: >
        Does the read sound like a person who knows the subject, or like a narrator reading? Are
        captions aligned to the final mix rather than approximated?

  hard_fails:
    # TIGHTENED 2026-08-19, and the wording is the whole of it. This used to read "does not
    # trace to a verified claim", which a judge showed is satisfied by a claim's `statement` or
    # `value_text` -- fields a model writes after reading the source. The film printed a readout
    # row against a claim marked VERIFIED whose fetched quote contained no such figure at all,
    # and every numeral gate stayed green because the numeral was in the authorised set.
    # Measured across that board, five of eleven readout figures sat in no fetched sentence.
    # The evidence is the QUOTE. `super_evidence_check` enforces this over supers and readouts,
    # with a per-claim `quote_is_excerpt` for sources that publish a table, declared rather than
    # inferred. This is a tightening, never a loosening: nothing that passed before on real
    # fetched evidence fails now.
    - a numeral on screen or in the script that does not appear in the fetched QUOTE of a
      verified claim, rather than merely in a statement or value_text written about it; the sole
      exception is a licence-version numeral inside the music.py-generated credit when
      music.py --verify-package binds that exact credit to a verified registry row
    - a caption timing that was approximated, scaled or hand-shifted rather than force-aligned
    - audio time-stretched to fit a cut
    - a region that does not match the story's county
    - a retired motif: six flags, Confederate imagery, lotería, calavera, a headdress
    - a brimmed hat on a rig floor or in a unit
    - a held slide longer than five seconds with no motion, emotion or revelation
    - a narrated idea that is not bound to an actual rendered item and visible change
    - a lead film that falls through to the generic plane renderer with no registered
      cinematic_template, physical throughline, performed turn, bookend and sourced sign-off

{
  "version": "dispatch-quality/1",
  "effective_date": "2026-09-27",
  "criteria": {
    "subject_recognition": "The principal subject is immediately recognizable at actual phone size, with enough picture space to understand its action.",
    "contact_and_consequence": "Objects have visible support and continuous identity; contact produces the depicted change, with a completed readable result.",
    "dominant_action": "The focal subject performs the narrated transformation. Peripheral motion, an overlay label or camera drift cannot supply missing action.",
    "surface_finish": "Inspect native detail as well as phone size. Surfaces, thickness, joints, light and shadows must look finished for the chosen style.",
    "continuity": "Each cut conserves a recognizable subject or explicitly introduces a sourced example; do not imply stock illustration is the actual case.",
    "closing_payoff": "The closing image answers the opening question and makes the source limit understandable without inventing a case outcome.",
    "sound": "Use actual audible-media evidence for voice, masking, sync and motivated sound. Never infer a listening verdict from captions."
  },
  "review_rule": "Ground blocking findings in a timed observed defect and its effect on comprehension or finish. Distinguish uncertainty and optional preferences without weakening mandatory standards. Readable evidence and completed-result holds are judged for their purpose; continuous motion alone earns no approval. A weakest interval is required even for a passing film. A preference for another style is not itself a blocking defect. Existing rubric hard fails, cinematic requirements and source limits remain mandatory."
}

# Finite creative repair and autonomous shipment

Owner instruction from October 3rd, 2026. Read knowledge/craft/AUTONOMOUS_COMPLETION.md before applying older resource-boundary language below. Internal review ceilings and host capacity errors trigger autonomous mandatory completion recovery, never an approval stop or an unfinished-capacity final response. Preserve exact failures, the original frozen envelope and cumulative charges. Only accepted finish --result shipped completes production.

Current modern-film policy has precedence over the generic deferrals below. For editions
selected by config/modern_film.json, its nondeferrable_categories and all required timed
observations remain mandatory, including pacing, motion, surface finish and ending artistry.
Read MODERN_FILM.md and STORY_ART.md before classifying those findings. A creative ceiling
ends optional polish; it cannot waive these floors or missing guide/source review coverage.
Use the existing source-backed mandatory recovery with the original evidence and charges.

Effective September 29, 2026. The owner requires a shipped video and prohibits stopping for
creative approval. The default limit is three creative repair rounds. Before September 30, each charged
`reboards` unit counts; later editions use the independently classified accounting below. Also stop optional creative
repair earlier after at least one repair and three critic calls when the effective frozen
critic ceiling has fewer than three calls left for another complete correction path. This
protects the final timed-phone review. The controller never resets or silently expands usage.

At that boundary, preserve the strongest reviewed complete cut and finish voice, measured
captions, native hero, final render, every independent audiovisual lens and the three scorers.
Do not start another aesthetic reboard. Correct retained factual or technical failures within
the recorded resources; do not reinterpret them as artistic or declare an incomplete delivery
shipped. Preserve real access/resource failures and continue the executable completion work.

The rubric, score and original pass/revise values remain unchanged. Only motion, surface
finish, pacing polish, ending artistry and style can be deferred. Source accuracy, rights,
readability, comprehension and misleading implications cannot. Native picture occupancy,
current renderer/film hashes, actual audible access, observation coverage, audio measurements,
caption alignment and every delivery gate continue to run. A missing review is never an
artistic defect. Structural motion-floor failures retain their original failed reports; native
proof retains measured failures in `bounded_creative_findings`.

An independent critic can classify an existing exact rejected report in a separate sidecar:

```sh
python scripts/creative_release.py --template --board out/dispatch/storyboard.json --report out/dispatch/phone-critic-current.json --film out/dispatch/openings/b.mp4 --scope phone
python scripts/creative_release.py --board out/dispatch/storyboard.json --report out/dispatch/phone-critic-current.json --scope phone
```

The first command produces a deliberately unapproved template under `creative-assessments`.
Only the original independent reviewer fills its observations and categories after examining
the retained evidence. Bind a preserved film/report path that later retiming cannot overwrite.
Every exact original blocker and failed phone observation must be classified once; unknown or
non-artistic categories refuse release. Retained checks need affirmative observed evidence.
The assessment binds the original report bytes, film, source claims and creative concept.
Keep all original reports untouched. Changes to source, concept or film need current evidence.

New provider/scorer responses include an honest `bounded_release` classification in their
initial immutable response. Obtain all lenses even if the first rejects. The audiovisual tool
adds the classification prompt; scorers read this policy and the same schema helper. A rejected
phone/AV report without concrete defects cannot use a score-only claim. A below-bar panel may
use score-only classification only when it has no separate rejected attention criterion.

`finish --result publishable` records the distinct publication mode and original failures in
controller `bounded_release`; it leaves production active in publishing. The final report card
still carries its genuine score, `ship` value and hard fails. Delivery copies assessments and
their exact rejected evidence. A passing later panel does not conceal earlier artistic
deferrals. `first_panel` success stays false if the panel actually failed.

Completion still requires exact-head CI, merge, deployment, permanent reviewed media bytes,
canonical phone playback through Computer Use, and a correctly addressed unsent Gmail draft
with readback. Only `finish --result shipped` completes production. No approval question or
new paid review is needed merely to classify retained evidence in the existing review scope.

## Accounting and quality correction from September 30, 2026

The three-round cap counts creative corrections. Technical repairs still consume the same
charged reboards, critic calls and frozen resources, but a predeclared technical-integrity
scope does not spend a creative round. The full-path headroom brake still counts all work;
this distinction adds no allowance. Historical editions retain their original accounting.

Before begin-repair, the existing independent critic's exact failure report must include
technical_repair.findings. Each row contains the exact original finding and one category:
source, rights, legibility, layout, technical_audio, captions or runtime. Every original
finding must be covered exactly once, by a reviewer distinct from the director. Motion,
pacing, story and style remain creative. Set repair_scope to technical-integrity in the plan.
Its evidence hash and scope are fixed before edits and checked again at authorization.
Only one reboard per such batch is excluded from creative count; all other charges count.

The finite rule ends optional polish on a credible treatment. It cannot waive a held-slide
structural motion failure or a failed dominant-action observation in new editions.
The known whole-film editorial-v1 screenshot/box treatment and repeated cut directions
are rejected before spending. Use the accepted complete preview as the finishing baseline.
If the initial comparison fails, change the mechanism promptly within the reserved path;
do not spend the remaining budget classifying the same wholesale failure as optional polish.
Keep the original score and rejection when a genuinely limited artistic shortfall is released.
Never ask for creative approval, reset usage, or claim shipment before its real evidence.
files.knowledge/craft/CREATIVE_DIRECTION.md:
# Story-led cinematic direction

Effective September 29, 2026; config/creative_production.json owns the date and version.
Earlier editions retain their original contracts. This policy replaces the dimensional opening
and runtime quota. All source, quality, independent review, native output, audio, caption,
budget and shipment requirements remain. It adds no score threshold or review role.

## Visual storytelling correction from October 2nd, 2026

Read [the visual-storytelling selector](visual-storytelling/README.md) and the selected approach
dossier in full before boarding. Choose observed documentary, explanatory animation,
evidence-led imagery or a cinematic scene from the source-backed action and available assets.
Variety is a tie-breaker between suitable approaches, not a weekday quota.

For newly planned editions from October 3rd, also read the [viewer planning method](visual-storytelling/viewer-plan.md).
Choose News report, Educational explainer or Cinematic scene as a format, then name the primary
approach in medium_choice. Record why it fits the inspected assets, the plausible alternative,
likely false inference and information sequence in the existing creative-direction, scene and
transition fields. For a report read [news-reporting.md](visual-storytelling/news-reporting.md)
and choose its structure from the sourced action. A format is not a mandatory presenter or
fixed rundown. A chosen guide is not a new quality criterion or approval field.

Complete the [sentence-to-shot worksheet](visual-storytelling/sentence-to-shot.md) in existing
creative-direction notes and the compact critic packet. Give each spoken clause a recognizable
pictured subject, visible relationship or action, inspectable result, source limit and connection
to the next shot. Do not add a new board schema, scoring weight, reviewer or render reservation.

The existing phone critic identifies the pictured input, action and result from the actual preview
before reading the director's explanation. Then it compares those observations with the spoken
clauses. A moving source-related prop is insufficient if a viewer can't recognize what it
represents. Missing or contradictory explanation stays a comprehension/source defect under the
current contract; decorative motion can't turn it into a deferrable style issue.

Retain the same two-treatment batch, frozen budget, native hero, independent reviews and
bounded-release route. The [October 2nd pavement diagnosis](visual-storytelling/october-2-pavement-case.md)
is a sampled-frame case study, not a replacement verdict or permission to alter the shipped film.

## Treatment recovery from September 30, 2026

September 29 is a rejected creative reference. Its source screenshots, repeated fading boxes
and growing underlines never became an engaging film. Use the source to discover a physical
task, obstacle and consequence. Preserve that action in the script and pictures. Authentic
imagery earns a shot when it reveals something; a relevant document is not automatically
the film's subject. Original source-grounded illustration and demonstrated action remain
first-class choices. Reuse proven components, never prior-edition photographic assets.

Start with one credible demonstrated treatment and one genuinely different visual treatment.
Compare their action, composition and viewer payoff in the existing batch. If both fail,
use one consolidated mechanism-changing simplification before narration; do not keep tuning
the same weak presentation. Preserve the strongest accepted complete preview as the fallback.
No extra research pass, reviewer role, third speculative concept or bespoke rig is authorized.

The existing critic must judge the whole film against the prior successful visual standard.
Named cities, correct labels and readable source text do not establish strong picture or place.
A code pass for geometry and provenance does not establish an engaging treatment. Inspect
the opening, middle and ending as actual action before refining layout. Give each cut its own
visible reason; repeated prose cannot direct ten different shots.

## Choose the story from its tangible stakes

Before narration, selected.visual_stakes records affected_person, physical_subject,
visible_change, consequence, opening_question, answer, asset_fit and source_urls. Name the
specific worker, resident or group and what changes for them. Tie the opening question to the
answer that the available evidence can support. A large announcement without useful pictures
is a weaker candidate than a smaller action with a visible consequence.

Inspect the real site, equipment, people, workflow and records during the existing bounded
visual search. Prefer the most informative authentic image. Apply the no-repeat policy in
DAILY_PRODUCTION.md. Use source-still or source-excerpt candidate rows with asset_url and the
same inspection/rights evidence as source-footage. Diagram rows need a sourced relationship
and disclosure Illustration. These are additional media, not permission to invent a workflow.

## Choose the medium from the evidence

Set cinema.version from the new policy. Keep hero_scene_id, optional hero_passage_end_scene_id,
visible_action, human_consequence and source_limit. dimensional_scene_ids is an exact inventory
of the quality_plan scenes using 3D; an empty list is legitimate. Each scene still needs a
filmable subject, action, consequence and source_basis. Geometry is useful when depth or contact
explains something. Footage is useful when the action is actually visible. A still can establish
a real place; an excerpt can expose the decisive words; a diagram can explain a sourced relation.
Do not force a character into a source image or draw a fake room to meet a quota.

The editorial-v1 route accepts each scene's picture with id, medium, event_id, disclosure and
subject (the inspected subject, checked by the critic). Use camera_strategy sourcePicture and
empty planes for this route's non-dimensional scenes. visual_proof.must_show binds picture.id.
Footage/stills/excerpts require file and sha256 from native_media; footprint, provenance and
rights remain mandatory. Footage also supplies trim_start_s, trim_end_s, creator, source_url,
license_url or its existing editorial_excerpt evidence. It plays at original speed with its
original audio muted. Deliberate environmental audio is separately sourced and mixed.

A crop is static x/y percentages. A focus box uses x/y/width/height percentages of the displayed
frame and reveals on event_id. Use it to reveal a real detail, never imply a machine detected it.
Source-excerpt renders the actual inspected page image, preserving its words. Diagram nodes
carry short label and claim_id; two to four nodes appear on the event clock. The source and
numeral gates cover those printed labels. No long paragraphs or substitute dashboards.
Dimensional scenes omit picture and call the existing demonstrated action route; bespoke
source-backed mechanisms retain their admission and native-hero requirements.

Every current scene receives full-resolution normal/subject-removed sample pairs. The existing
proof key without_stage now removes the principal picture for each medium. It never removes
captions or branding to manufacture visible action. A source still/excerpt may have a justified
intentional_hold within the policy duration after the opening; the phone and final lenses still
judge its purpose. Otherwise the principal picture must visibly develop on its event clock.
The hero remains a finished native passage with sound, even when it uses no 3D.

## Compare two openings once

Prepare opening-a.json and opening-b.json beside storyboard.json. From September 30, both may
change the complete visual treatment, including the middle and ending. Keep the same dated
facts, narration, scene ids and timing, shared inspected asset set and viewer question. Their
full visual concepts are hash-bound, including body scenes; retiming does not change identity.
For September 29 captures only, the original first-scene-only comparison remains reproducible.
Make genuinely different visual approaches. Keep both inside the source and medium contracts.
The existing independent code critic reviews both in one reserved assignment and returns
opening-a-critic.json and opening-b-critic.json using the ordinary exact concept/renderer/story
bindings. It can reject both before a render is spent. Do not add another reviewer identity.

Run scripts/opening_compare.py once. It reserves one preflight batch, renders exactly two
quarter-scale full animatics with one browser/bundle, and saves openings/comparison.json.
Both completed films receive exact-board, film, renderer and inspector-bound structural reports
before phone review. The comparison retains both reports and all failures, even if the first
inspection fails. Cached comparisons inspect the retained bytes without another render. The
normal command exits nonzero on inspection failure. Its --retain-failed-inspection flag retains
diagnostics for policy-authorized finishing only; it does not change a failed report or approve
phone review. These inexpensive options share the same narrative, so the chosen full preview is
already available for continuity review. Failed attempts stay charged. A changed batch requires
the existing consolidated repair path, never an automatic reset.

For a retained capture from the reviewed pre-inspection orchestration version, use
opening_compare.py --inspect-retained. This performs no render or reservation. It verifies the
known original orchestration hash, every unchanged capture dependency, both original films and
boards, the renderer and source assets, and the original charged reservation. It archives the
original comparison and keeps its producer hash, then binds new inspection reports separately.
The existing independent selection may keep its original comparison hash only while the exact
original capture record is unchanged. Unknown capture versions or changed dependencies refuse
adoption. Failed measurements remain failed under this path too.

The existing exact-phone critic watches both openings, then the chosen whole sequence. It writes
openings/selection.json with comparison_sha256, selected (a or b), director_identity,
reviewer_identity, reason, rejected_reason and blocking_defects. Reasons describe observed
pixels and the opening question. Copy the chosen frozen board to storyboard.json and its film
to preflight.mp4; retain its matching code critique as storyboard_critic.json, inspect that exact
film with preflight_animatic --inspect-only, then record the ordinary phone verdict on those
bytes. The unused option stays as evidence. Neither option authorizes a narration take until
the chosen cut passes the current phone gate. No third concept or extra panel by default.

## Direct performance, sound and cuts together

creative_direction binds policy_sha256 and records viewer_question, visible_answer,
emotional_turn and medium_choice. Its ordered edits rows contain scene_id, enter_on, leave_on,
cut_after_event_id and next_connection. The actual event must complete before the cut; a prose
promise cannot substitute for its clock. Describe the visible instant that earns each cut and the carried subject
or sourced relationship. The final row states the resolved answer and source limit. After any
structural change, review the whole sequence. Measured narration retimes the event clock; do not
add dead air to preserve an arbitrary grid or accelerate the voice to rescue too many words.

creative_direction.sound records perspective, music_arc, voice_arc and cues. Each cue has id,
event_id, role (environment, contact, sonification or quiet), duration_s, intent and provenance.
Use truthful recorded ambience or an explicitly designed effect. Do not pretend a generated
sound was recorded at the actual site. Avoid a hit at every cut. Include one deliberate background
contrast with a quiet cue and gain from the policy contract. The quiet cue reduces the music and
effects bus on its actual visual event; it never mutes, stretches or splices the narration.

Each non-quiet cue has one sfx_events entry with matching id/event_id, wav, source and gain.
The mixer anchors it to the current board event, trims to its declared duration at original
speed, adds short edge fades and refuses undersized or nonfinite audio. It records every cue,
source WAV hash and the exact sound/timing digest in mix.json. Retime the sfx event file with the
board and remix after a changed clock. Old mix evidence fails the release check.

The existing voice director reads this sound arc and the selected opening. It binds
sound_direction_sha256 to the sound object and gives each line specific intent, relative energy
and an exact spoken emphasis phrase. Contrast curiosity, discovery and the final consequence
without a trailer voice. Numeric pause commands stay out of the TTS prompt. One continuous take
and its existing audible soundcheck remain the default; field completion cannot approve a flat
or synthetic read. The sound lens judges actual delivery, masking, sync and contrast in the MP4.

All three final audiovisual lenses and scoring agents remain. The legacy response field
dimensional_action describes the principal picture in any medium. A judge may reject a weak
image, inert diagram, generic read or unearned cut with timestamped evidence; a medium preference
alone is not a defect. Passing quality moves directly to release and verified shipment.

## What you are looking for

**Genuine divergence, not a relabel.** Two scenes that both say "wide establishing shot" with
different nouns are one scene twice. Composition, camera move, scale and subject must actually
differ.

**Film-level construction.** Count `visual_family` and `payload_mode`, not just scene signatures.
Two families carrying most of the runtime or a sequence of figures delivered as text panels is a
structural ceiling. Props cannot repair it later.

**The early payoff is a picture.** Read its deadline from `config/documentary.json`.
Scene one names a real strategy and visible payoff. An establishing shot, title, or promise
that something will become interesting later is not a hook.

**Picture-led.** Follow the action with the narration and labels covered. If the story
only works with narration, it is a podcast with pictures and it fails here.

**Input is not processing proof.** If narration describes scanning, analyzing, selecting or another transformation, a captured input image alone does not prove that action. The current phone film must show the transformation and a completed visible consequence in the same objects. Captions may explain scope; they cannot supply a missing action. A retained still can be valid evidence, but an unchanged inset is not an analysis beat. Compare the native rejection interval with the new phone pixels before approving the same mechanism again.

**Judge the dominant picture, not peripheral motion.** A small moving sliver behind a large static inset does not repair the inset's pacing. Inspect the actual native hero at phone size and native crop scale: recognizable silhouettes at 270 pixels can conceal unfinished surfaces, faceted props and missing contact shadows. Compare all unresolved native defects together before the next render; do not approve a label, outline or tiny prop change as a complete repair. If the same dominant layout has failed twice, require a changed composition or action mechanism before another native attempt.

**Sentence-to-pixel proof.** Ignore `on_screen`, `what_moves` and `hero` on the first pass. For
each VO line, inspect `visual_proof.must_show`, resolve every `item_id` into `planes[].items`, and
ask whether those actual components and props make the sentence literal. A generic pickup under a
readout is not a model joining records. If the binding is technically present but visually tiny
or dominated by unrelated context, revise it.

**Docket flow.** The scene roles should cause one another: movement, consequence, honest limit,
then agency. A list of facts can be accurate and still have no story. The close should answer
"what happens next" rather than merely restate the hook.

**Attention earns each interval.** Read `config/documentary.json` and the craft guide. Resolve
`attention_beats` through the scene event ids, including the gap to the ending. The hook must
actually pay off within the policy window. A line of text, a camera drift or an animated dash
cannot rescue a subject that does nothing. The faster direction asks for action, consequence,
evidence or human response while preserving time to understand each idea.

**Motivated framing.** The camera can hold while a subject acts or evidence is read. Move it to
reveal a relationship, follow an action or change the viewer's understanding. Do not add orbiting
or zooming merely to advertise the engine. A continuous action may span multiple scene records.

**Three images before a finished film.** Identify the opening payoff, central mechanism and
closing consequence. Ask which image will be remembered and what question it resolves. If these
are three cards with labels, reboard before spending a render. Check the actual source of every
reconstruction and whether its visual certainty exceeds the reporting.

**Visual access before visual promises.** For each of those three images, name the public
reference or source fact that permits its depiction. If the pivotal action occurs inside a
private interface, lab or workplace that no source shows, do not approve a sequence of invented
screens and pointing gestures as observed workflow. Require an explicitly illustrated mechanism
whose state visibly changes, or send the director back to a more filmable source-backed angle.
An event list with verbs is insufficient when the same generic panel remains the dominant image.

**Region correctness.** The scene's region comes from the story's county. A board that puts a Hill
Country palette on a Panhandle story is wrong before it is drawn.

Return the complete bound gate-ready report described above. The fields `verdict`, `notes`,
`strongest_frame` and `weakest_frame` are part of that report, not a substitute for its bindings,
`story_review`, action reviews or the timed phone and modern observations required at phone scope.

`weakest_frame` is required. Every board has one and naming it is more useful than praise.

Actor orientation must support the action: an inspector examining a house must visibly attend to the house or its image, rather than face the audience while pointing behind the body. Grounded weight shifts need planted feet and articulated hips or knees; rotating an entire rigid figure is not a performed stance change.

tools and carried object, and verify a shared ground. Sample upper-arm and forearm lengths
through the complete performance. Arbitrary curved tubes, stretched reach and silent target
clamping can preserve contact while breaking believable motion. A supported prop or clear
silhouette alone cannot clear those defects. Inspect actual native surface and motion quality
after the phone pass; keep those two review scopes explicit.

**Review the occupied picture space.** Check the principal subject at the beginning, contact,
and result of each event against the actual shared caption band and title overlays. Inspect
phone frames at all three moments, not only a representative contact-sheet frame. A moving
object whose landing is hidden by captions fails even if its path is visible. The ending of an
action must remain readable long enough to explain the next shot.
