# Make the editorial choice before the picture

Apply this method to newly planned editions from October 3rd, 2026. It guides decisions under the current contracts and does not certify quality. It adds no board schema, scorer, research pass or paid attempt.

## Decide and record

Read the selector and chosen approach dossier in full. For a news report also read the reporting dossier. Use the existing creative_direction and story_contract fields; keep the decision rationale compact and inspectable.

1. **Focus.** In viewer_question and visible_answer, state what changes, for whom, through which sourced action. Name the expected viewer takeaway and the strongest honest limit. Distinguish the narrative answer from an unknown eventual outcome.
2. **Choose.** Begin medium_choice with the named format and approach: News report, Educational explainer or Cinematic scene; then Observed documentary, Explanatory animation, Evidence-led imagery or Cinematic scene. Explain why the available assets can carry the explanation and why a plausible alternative is weaker. Naming an approach is a routing aid, not an approval field.
3. **Order.** Put each beat's reporting job in the existing scene advances and edit notes. For a report choose human-led, mechanism-led or evidence-led ordering. Explain why this evidence appears here and what question it creates or answers. Educational explanation builds a recognizable example through successive states. A cinematic scene follows a task, obstacle, consequential turn and completed action. Do not apply one rundown to all three.
4. **Anticipate confusion.** Name the most likely false inference and the picture or immediate source limit that prevents it. In emotional_turn, connect the viewer's changing understanding to an evidenced stake. Do not invent a person's feelings or claim to know the audience's reaction.
5. **Connect.** In enter_on, leave_on, cut_after_event_id and next_connection, name the visible event, new information and carried subject. Complete the event before the cut. A footage-to-diagram handoff keeps the same identified example or discloses a new one. Finish the sentence-to-shot worksheet inside these existing notes.
6. **Direct and test.** Tie line intent, emphasis, motivated sound and captions to the actual reveal. Before spending, ask what remains understandable with narration muted and editorial labels covered, then test the combined account. Essential dates and attribution can use text; the principal action must read in the picture. Budget the entire remaining review/render path, including independent-provider recovery where required.

These are short decision reasons a colleague can inspect, not a request for a private stream of thought. Use concrete evidence and an alternative that could realistically be built. Do not fill every field with the same sentence, duplicate the research or commission a third treatment.

## Each worker has a distinct decision

- **Researcher:** Identify the most informative picture and the strongest limitation. Recommend an angle that the assets can actually show; flag the sentence for which no truthful picture exists.
- **Director:** Choose the story focus, format, medium and order. Resolve the weak handoff before narration, using the same two-treatment batch and consolidated ledger.
- **VO director:** Translate the approved beat jobs into a continuous performance. Explain a lift, drop or pause through the reveal it supports; preserve the words and alignment.
- **Code critic:** Determine whether the proposed implementation can perform the action and carry the explanation. A planned gesture is not a watched result.
- **Phone critic and scorers:** First describe what is recognizable and what changes in the actual film. Then compare with the approved account. Locate the weakest identity or information handoff and classify the observed defect under the existing criteria. Keep their separate assigned lenses and actual verdicts.

For remote independent recovery, the supplied packet contains the actual method, selector, reporting dossier and named approach text. If a director has not named an approach, all four approach guides are supplied rather than pretending an unread local path was available. The new teaching bundle is added only for editions from October 3rd. A text packet never establishes audiovisual access.

## Why the handoff needs thought

An original film-comprehension study associated event boundaries with meaningful changes in characters, objects, place, goals and causes. Our application is to preserve those relationships across a cut and make a change understandable. This is an editorial inference, not a scientifically established short-video pacing interval or retention guarantee. [Zacks and colleagues, The Brain's Cutting-Room Floor](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/human-neuroscience/articles/10.3389/fnhum.2010.00168/full).

The director can consult the [observed news examples](broadcast-cadence-study.md) when a reporting choice needs a model. Workers use the supplied method, relevant guide and current artifacts without repeatedly reloading the research corpus. Retain real rejections; a well-written plan can't clear absent action, false implication or failed comprehension.

# Visual storytelling for Dispatch

Research and direction revision: October 2nd, 2026.

The picture, narration and captions must describe the same unfolding story. The picture supplies a recognizable subject, relationship, action or consequence. Narration explains its significance and limits. Captions give access to the spoken account. A moving object is useful only when the viewer understands what it represents and what its change means.

These dossiers combine researched craft with proposed Dispatch practice. Source observations are identified and linked. The shot methods, selection procedure and worked example are our production recommendations, not claims that research guarantees audience engagement.

## Choose the story's visual approach

Read this index and the chosen dossier in full before boarding. Select by the available evidence and the explanation the viewer needs. Keep one primary approach; supporting footage or documents should connect to that approach through a clear subject or question.

| Approach | Choose when | What it must show | Reject when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Observed documentary](observed-documentary.md) | Authenticated footage shows the actual people, place, equipment or workflow | A real action and its observed result | Similar-looking stock replaces the story's actual identity |
| [Explanatory animation](explanatory-animation.md) | The central process or comparison is hard to see directly | Recognizable input, meaningful transformation and readable output | Abstract objects require a private legend to decode |
| [Evidence-led imagery](evidence-led-imagery.md) | Relevant photographs or documents carry the reporting | What the evidence establishes and how it changes the answer | A sequence of screenshots substitutes for the entire mechanism |
| [Cinematic scene](cinematic-scene.md) | A source-backed physical task, obstacle and consequence can sustain a scene | Spatially coherent action, a turn and a consequential ending | Lighting, orbiting props or music replace story development |

Use this selection order:

1. State the viewer's question, sourced action, affected person or group and honest ending.
2. Inventory inspected, usable assets and demonstrated components. Record what each can and can't show.
3. Choose the approach that makes the central relationship easiest to understand. Explain the rejected alternative in one sentence.
4. Complete the [sentence-to-shot worksheet](sentence-to-shot.md). Resolve missing pictures before locking narration.
5. Compare exactly two genuinely different complete treatments in the existing shared preview batch. Read the selected dossier for each treatment. Preserve the current contracts, frozen budget and existing independent roles.
6. Have the existing critic inspect the actual rendered sequence before reading the director's explanation. A filled worksheet does not prove comprehension.

Do not impose a weekday rotation. Track the selected approach in the existing creative-direction rationale so the director can see recent repetition. When two approaches fit equally well, variety can break the tie. Never choose variety at the expense of truth or comprehension.

## Choose a format and think through its sequence

For newly planned editions from October 3rd, read the [viewer planning method](viewer-plan.md) in full. Distinguish the format from the medium: a news report can use observed footage, illustration or documents; an educational explainer can return from a diagram to physical evidence; a cinematic scene still needs a truthful task and consequence.

For a news report read [the reporting dossier](news-reporting.md) and choose its human-led, mechanism-led or evidence-led structure from the actual story. Record why the order works, the likely false inference and the carried subject across each cut in the existing creative-direction and transition fields. The [national-news study](broadcast-cadence-study.md) identifies the observed examples and access limits. It does not prescribe a single bracketed rundown.

The director and workers use these short decision reasons to choose and challenge the treatment. A copied structure, named style or completed worksheet supplies no quality verdict. The packet tools bind the current method and relevant approach text; remote recovery supplies the actual text because a provider can't open local links.

## Give the three channels distinct jobs

**See:** Show the thing being discussed at the moment it is discussed. Preserve its identity across the cut. Make any comparison legible before asking the viewer to infer a result.

**Hear:** Name the relationship, cause or uncertainty that the picture can't establish alone. Time emphasis and event sound to the actual reveal. A music swell can't supply an unreported outcome.

**Read:** Retain complete measured captions. Use brief object labels only where they identify a picture or distinction. Avoid simultaneous paragraph copy competing with both the action and captions. Lay out the decisive result above the real caption band and hold it long enough to understand.

Mayer's research summary supports removing distracting content, placing related words near pictures and presenting corresponding animation and narration together. It also reports redundancy effects in multimedia learning. These are learning findings, not a forecast of short-video retention; they do not justify removing accessible captions. Our application is to reduce competing editorial text while maintaining captions. [Cambridge multimedia-learning chapter](https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/abs/cambridge-handbook-of-multimedia-learning/principles-for-reducing-extraneous-processing-in-multimedia-learning-coherence-signaling-redundancy-spatial-contiguity-and-temporal-contiguity-principles/C98AB3A6CE760DD63C048936EA0B3B44), [W3C caption guidance](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/captions-prerecorded).

## Review what the viewer receives

Use the existing review assignments and fixed rubric. Add these observations to their existing consolidated notes, not a new scorecard or paid role.

- **Recognition:** Before reading the board, what does the principal object look like? Can the critic name it without guessing?
- **Alignment:** At each narrated clause, does the picture show the named subject and relationship? Record exact film times for contradictions or absent concepts.
- **Development:** What changed, and how does that change lead to the next shot? Distinguish subject transformation from decorative motion.
- **Continuity:** Is the same person, site, sample or document being followed? Is a different example disclosed?
- **Combined comprehension:** After one viewing with audio and captions, what happened, who can act and what remains unproven?
- **Picture contribution:** With narration muted and captions covered, which parts of the central process can the viewer actually see? Dates and attribution may rely on text; the principal action can't.
- **Ending:** Does the final picture answer the opening question without inventing implementation, savings, approval or repair?

An unrecognizable object, absent principal action or contradictory picture is a comprehension/source defect under the current contract. Do not classify it as merely style because pixels move. Surface polish and optional camera preferences remain artistic issues. Retain all real rejected verdicts and use the existing repair and bounded-release policies.

## Apply this without expanding production

Use the current budget precheck for the complete review and render path before spending. Keep the bounded visual search, source and rights evidence, prior-edition identity gate, two-treatment comparison, native hero, phone inspection, audiovisual lenses and independent scorers. The dossiers introduce no render quota, new reviewer or budget extension.

Read [the October 2nd diagnosis and proposed sequence](october-2-pavement-case.md) for the difference between a source-related object and a picture that communicates the spoken claim.

## Research status

Sources were accessed October 2nd, 2026. The four approach dossiers use published guidance, research summaries and practitioner accounts; their linked film examples are references rather than claimed viewing. The separate national-news study adds explicitly scoped transcripts and rendered samples. Today's diagnosis uses the listed native frame samples and retained board; it is not a replacement independent whole-film review. Research access does not grant reuse rights to any publisher's images, footage or soundtrack.

# Direct a coherent news report

The [cadence study](broadcast-cadence-study.md) records the evidence behind this dossier. The structures below are Dispatch production choices, not a universal network script. Apply them to newly planned editions from October 3rd, 2026; preserve shipped editions and their real reviews.

A report has an editorial spine: a specific situation, a question, evidence that changes the answer, an explanation, an honest consequence and a close. Decide which of those jobs the next shot performs. A source-related image that supplies no new understanding is a weak insert, even if its colors and motion look expensive.

## Choose the order from the story

| Reporting structure | Choose it when | Sequence of reporting jobs | Ending test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Human-led report | The evidence identifies a real person's task, obstacle or changed options | Show the task or consequence → establish the dated change → broaden with evidence → explain the cause and limits → return to the same person or task | Has the viewer learned what changes for that person, without an invented reaction or outcome? |
| Mechanism-led report | The central news is a process, measurement or decision that viewers can't readily see | Show a recognizable input and question → orient the source and setting → reveal the transformation → show the result → connect it to a human decision and its limits | Can the viewer explain the input, transformation and result, and distinguish an illustration from observed operation? |
| Evidence-led report | A filing, policy, measurement or public record changes the reported answer | Establish the dated decision or disputed claim → expose the decisive source detail → explain its effect with a concrete relationship → show affected options or activity → state the unresolved point and next decision | Does the ending answer what the record establishes, who can act next and what it does not establish? |

Choose one structure. Compress or reorder it when the evidence and viewer's question justify that choice. Establish the essential source limitation when the affected claim appears; a later caveat can't undo a misleading picture. Keep the current early-picture payoff and event timing requirements. These sequences introduce no extra scenes, prescribed shot seconds or runtime quota.

The CBS transcript in the study provides a specific-to-broad-to-specific example. The CNN transcript shows a different package organization, and the MSNBC example is a question-led interview. They are different forms with different access to people and evidence. A short Dispatch should not imitate a lengthy panel simply because it resembles national television.

## Assign each ingredient a reporting job

**Opening:** Give the viewer something identifiable to understand immediately: a task interrupted, an input changing, a decision confronting evidence, or a completed consequence that creates a question. State the actual question soon enough to guide the picture. A dramatic claim must stay within the fetched evidence. Do not borrow an unrelated victim, emergency or reaction to manufacture stakes.

**Orientation:** Establish who, where and what changed using the minimum needed narration and labels. This is the short-video equivalent of the paragraph that explains the focus of an article. The viewer should know why the next piece of evidence belongs in this story.

**Reporter or presenter:** Use an actual reusable field passage when it demonstrates, verifies or bridges the explanation. A fabricated journalist, microphone prop or studio cut adds no verification. Dispatch's narrator can orient the viewer without appearing as a reporter. A person on screen must have a source-backed role and perform an understandable action.

**Evidence:** Show the exact place, equipment, task, relevant photograph or decisive source words. Identify what the evidence establishes. A quotation is evidence of what its speaker said; it is not proof that their conclusion is true. Show a contrary finding or uncertainty when the story requires it. Use the existing source and rights lanes for every asset.

**Explanation:** Introduce coded visuals when they reveal a relationship that the authentic image can't show. Keep the same physical subject or explicitly identify the new example. The diagram should answer the question created by the preceding shot. Return to the source image or human decision after the explanation when that return completes the thought.

**Consequence and close:** Show how the action changes a state, choice, risk or next step. Answer the opening question through the completed visible action. Distinguish a demonstrated consequence, an expected effect and an unknown eventual outcome. Do not repeat the introduction merely to make the film seem circular. A return earns its place when the viewer now understands the original subject differently.

## Move between authentic pictures and coded explanation

Make each handoff explicit in the existing edit notes. Carry a stable identifying detail: the same road patch, sample, site, device, document passage or clearly disclosed example. Preserve orientation, useful scale and the relationship under explanation. An outline or highlight identifies a region; it does not prove that a machine detected, measured or classified it.

For example, an authenticated image can establish the input. An explicitly illustrated transformation can explain the source-supported relationship. A return to the actual task can show who uses the result. Cutting from an unrelated office image to anonymous blocks and then to a different city breaks that connection, even if every image is broadly about AI.

Original illustration is a valid principal medium. Useful footage is also valid. An irrelevant insert should be omitted within the existing bounded search. Do not commission an unproven rig or prolong the stock hunt to imitate a particular outlet. Use the current source-backed action admission when a genuinely necessary mechanism needs implementation.

## Direct the cadence across picture, voice and reading

Give each beat one new idea the viewer needs for the next beat. Complete its decisive event before cutting. Preserve enough time to recognize the subject, follow the change and read the result. Trim repeated setup before requesting faster narration. Pace varies with information and action; a cut on a fixed timer is not an editorial reason.

Voice should orient, reveal, explain, qualify or resolve. Tell the VO director which job a line performs and where the visual answer lands. Keep the approved continuous script and measured alignment. Use contrast in intent and emphasis rather than perpetual urgency. Do not turn a hypothesis into certainty through a triumphant delivery or sound cue.

Natural sound, verified interview audio and motivated effects can connect thoughts when their provenance and actual event timing support that use. A sound bridge can carry the same action over a cut. Sound can't imply recorded access to a site we did not visit. Preserve intelligibility and all existing audio checks.

Retain complete captions. Keep extra labels short and attached to the object they identify. Do not present a second paragraph, a busy diagram and a new location at the same time as a dense spoken sentence. Seeing, hearing and reading should reinforce the same unfolding account.

## Review the actual report

The existing critic and scorers reconstruct the story from the current film before consulting the director's rationale. They identify what the opening asks, what new information arrives in the middle, how subject identity survives each handoff, and what the ending answers. Then they compare that understanding with the approved words and fetched evidence.

Use exact intervals and the existing observation fields. A missing principal action, unrecognizable subject, false visual implication or failed explanation remains a source/comprehension failure under the current contract. Optional presenter preferences, shot polish and an alternative ordering alone do not create a new mandatory test. Keep the fixed rubric and retain every actual rejection.

# Evidence-led imagery

Read the [shared visual-storytelling direction](README.md) first.

## What this approach does

It lets the viewer examine real reporting evidence: a site photograph, source image, dated document, map or published result. It is useful when authentic footage is unavailable and the evidence has concrete visual content.

Choose it when the viewer's question concerns what a document establishes, where a change occurs, who is involved or what a photographed condition actually looks like. It can support an explanatory sequence; it must not turn an entire process story into reading screenshots.

## Research findings and limits

NPR Visuals describes sequential stories combining photography and text, sometimes with audio, video or illustration. Its retrospective reports varied completion performance and cautions that strong visuals and the story itself are essential. Those observations concern interactive web stories and do not establish short-video performance. [NPR's sequential-story analysis](https://blog.apps.npr.org/2015/11/19/sequential-visual-stories.html).

Reuters' standards require accurate images and attribution that identifies outside material's actual source. They prohibit fabrication and warn against visual changes that misrepresent reality. This supports honest identity and presentation; it does not grant licences for Reuters or other publishers' media. [Reuters standards](https://reutersagency.com/about/standards-values/).

## Dispatch method

Give every asset a specific evidentiary job. Before boarding, record the claim it supports, the detail the viewer will inspect, what lies outside its evidentiary scope, and its established reuse rights. A portrait identifies a person. A site image establishes visible conditions at its documented place and time. Neither proves an unseen workflow.

Arrange the evidence around a question:

| Stage | Picture function | Editing choice |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Orient | Show the actual site, subject or full source context | Hold a readable establishing view |
| Inspect | Reveal the one detail that supports the claim | A purposeful crop or highlight |
| Compare | Show a documented contrast, location or relationship | Matched views with honest identities |
| Establish scope | Identify date, issuer and limitation | A brief readable source passage |
| Return | Connect the evidence to the physical consequence | Return to the subject, changed understanding |

Each cut should answer the previous shot's question. Do not count a new excerpt, title or fade as a new development when it repeats the same information.

For a document, show enough context to establish its identity, then expose the decisive passage. Preserve surrounding qualifications that change the claim. An enlarged crop must not make a planned feature look delivered. Use an original explanatory panel when a truthful transcription is clearer, and disclose it; do not fabricate a screenshot.

For a photograph, keep the actual detail visible. Camera movement should reveal geography, scale or a relationship, not simply animate an inert image. Do not use a crop to imply a different place or eliminate context that changes interpretation. Do not animate a real still into an invented observed event.

## Pair evidence with explanation

If the story says a system processes data, a screenshot of its input supports the input claim only. To explain the transformation, pair it with a disclosed source-bound animation or authenticated output. Do not fill the rest of the film with underlines and excerpts because a source page is easy to obtain.

For the pavement story, a verified example of surface and range imagery could support a comparison. A university article supports attribution and date. It does not supply proof of a completed road repair. When usable technical images have no established rights, draw an explicitly conceptual explanation instead.

Keep complete captions in their measured band. A dense passage and a long spoken sentence can overload the phone frame; use only the necessary excerpt and preserve its source context in the existing evidence package. Narration should explain the visible detail rather than read an unrelated paragraph over it.

## Before voice and final review

The existing critic should explain what each asset proves and where the sequence implies more. Ask whether the film still has a principal action and consequence under the current contract. Reject the known whole-film screenshot-and-fading-box approach before spending.

Keep the prior-edition identity check, native asset provenance, rights evidence and normal phone review. If no useful external imagery is available, omit the insert and move on. The fallback must remain a complete explanatory treatment, not a stalled stock search.

# Direct the film before describing its look

Owner instruction, October 7th, 2026. Active for newly planned editions from October 8th,
or an explicit `film_direction` opt-in. The original source, rights, minimum action,
native PNG/CRF16, audio, caption, independent panel and autonomous shipment gates remain.

## What the previous upgrade failed to change

October 7th's shipped film passed its mechanical gates and scored 7.596. The owner rejected
its engagement and pace. It repeated an equipment tableau through six scenes, with a 9.5-second
closing scene. Palette, camera poses and declared events did not create a visual argument.
The bounded release contract could also defer pacing, motion, surface finish and ending artistry.
Neither a score nor a completed worksheet overrules that observed failure.

This upgrade therefore changes the executable route and review eligibility. It does not promise
an aesthetic result from a new renderer name. Current production uses `directed-film-v2` and a
registered, story-specific episode. Missing plans, unknown views and legacy routes fail. Older
episodes remain reproducible as historical evidence. A current film cannot defer the four
categories above, even at a creative ceiling. Capacity recovery funds mandatory repair on the
current route; it never restores the retired route or edits a rejected finding.

## Lessons verified in AlaskaAIWeekly

Study pinned source and complete published films, rather than an isolated hero still. The current
reference revision is `e53f3f92e6cbe123e8802239d8172622d4f3a630`.

- [Directors room](https://github.com/Talonsturgill/alaska-ai-weekly/blob/e53f3f92e6cbe123e8802239d8172622d4f3a630/prompts/dispatch_routine.md)
  commits an earned angle, cold open, escalation, performed turn and visual button. Translate its
  contrasting dramatic, comic, explanatory and curious lenses into the existing two complete
  Texas treatments. Do not add daily roles, extra pitches or another paid panel.
- [October 7th episode](https://github.com/Talonsturgill/alaska-ai-weekly/blob/e53f3f92e6cbe123e8802239d8172622d4f3a630/video-engine/src/Ep1007.tsx)
  uses a recurring physical object, distinct shot sizes, local reactions, carefully finished
  silhouettes and named visual reveals. A figure's state changes across scenes; the frame does
  not merely rescan the same equipment.
- [October 6th episode](https://github.com/Talonsturgill/alaska-ai-weekly/blob/e53f3f92e6cbe123e8802239d8172622d4f3a630/video-engine/src/Ep1006.tsx)
  gives its desk and phone a visual performance, with local anticipation, contact and result.
  Port that causal grammar and reusable finished assets. Do not copy its regional mascot,
  factual claims, source archive, ledger or old footage into Texas.
- The current Alaska master also corrects its old instruction to punctuate every beat with a
  camera kick. Preserve motivated cuts and object reactions. Frequent new information does not
  mean perpetual shake, strobing, overshoot or arbitrary camera motion.

## Two complete treatments, one executable direction

Before voice, design exactly two feasible, complete alternatives. Each needs a first-frame
question, a recognizable throughline subject, an escalation, a fair source-backed turn, a
closing picture that answers the opening, and a sound arc. Different shot ordering, staging
and visual emphasis must give a viewer a different experience. Two camera poses on the same
tableau are one treatment.

Write `film_direction` with the active policy version, registered episode, actual renderer
hashes, angle, opening promise, performed turn, closing answer, shot timeline and rewards.
The shot timeline covers every story frame, conserves subject identity and source-bound scene
timing, and names an implemented view and overlapping physical event. Use at least three useful
framings. A new action, reaction, comparison, consequence or evidence reveal earns each cut.
An empty push, rotating fan or appearing label alone does not count as new understanding.

Before code review, freeze each shot's `scene_fraction_start` and `scene_fraction_end` within its source
scene, and each reward's `event_fraction` within its physical event. These authored anchors
belong to the approved concept. `board_retime.py` derives the measured seconds from them after
voice alignment, without compounding earlier timing. If the measured read breaks the limits
or event overlap, repair the edit; never stretch the narration or silently move a reward.

The current product limits are in `config/modern_film.json`: first visible change within 1.5
seconds, no shot longer than 5 seconds, and no unearned information interval longer than 4
seconds. These are explicit production constraints chosen after the owner rejection, not a
scientific claim about all audiences. Do not bypass them by relabeling a repeated view or
inventing event declarations. Independent review watches the execution at normal speed.

Generate this edition's fresh hero and supporting artwork under STORY_ART.md before animation.
Finish the hero silhouette, contact shadows, layered surfaces, motivated light and focal hierarchy
at native size and 390-pixel phone width before voice. Use authentic licensed footage when it
provides useful action. Otherwise author a source-bound illustration. Do not infer a particular
failure mechanism, measured value, actual operator, hardware design or completed outcome.

## Perform and judge the complete edit

Narration is an energetic, continuous explanation with purposeful contrasts. Begin the action
immediately, keep connective phrases moving, and reserve emphasis and breathing room for the
turn and answer. Do not put a reverent pause after every clause. Shorten slow writing before
synthesis, rather than accelerating the audio. Compare actual take timing with the approved
shot rewards and listen through the existing audiovisual path. Fast unreadable words fail too.

The existing phone critic and three separate final scorers receive this guide's actual text and
hash. At visual/final scope each returns exact-film `modern_observations` for first frame, visual
progression, shot variety, performed turn, pace, closing answer and finished art. Each contains
an observed interval, concrete finding and pass flag. The ordinary rubric and actual failures
remain unchanged. A high average cannot replace a failed engagement or finish observation.

Optional engineering stops at its reserved boundary. If a mandatory current-route observation
fails, preserve that cut and repair through the configured autonomous completion policy, using
the retained independent source-backed pivot when needed. Neither artistic ceilings nor host
capacity authorize a legacy episode, slideshow rescue or unaudited provider substitution.


## The region stands behind every current film

Owner instruction, October 9th, 2026, on the plan's fifth step. Place was the show's weakest axis
(6.36 on the mean of the last ten report cards) and every current film stood in a flat gradient,
so a Harris County story and a Reeves County story looked like the same nowhere.

From the date in `video-engine/src/modern/placePlates.json` (`policy.effective_date`), DirectedFilm
draws each scene's region behind its episode through `modern/PlaceStage.tsx`. Each of the ten
regions has a plate, rendered once in the Docket's carousel engine from a scene page under
`assets/place/scenes/` by `scripts/place_bake.py`, as a sky, one ground and cards for the things
standing on it. The bake measured that the layers reassemble into the picture and that every
camera profile keeps the ground covering the frame and every base on its ground. The manifest
records those measurements, the Docket commit, every layer's sha256 and the hash of each module a
scene imports from `assets/place/`. Water is drawn by `assets/place/water.js` as a mirror of the
world in its own plane, because a lake seen from eye height under a hazy sky otherwise reads as a
pale slab, and no scatter grows on it.

- **The plate is the county's when it has one, and the region's when it doesn't.** A region's own
  plate carries nothing that belongs to one place, no skyline and no refinery, because a Texan is
  not told they live somewhere they don't. Harris County stands in Houston across Buffalo Bayou,
  Dallas County over the Trinity floodplain, Travis County across Lady Bird Lake and Bexar County
  over the river south of downtown. A story at a plant on the upper coast names
  `place_plate: "gulf-shipchannel"` on its scenes for the refineries, which a board may do only for
  a county that plate lists. The fly gene film's labs are in the Medical Center, and a blind grade
  of its frames on October 9th marked the refinery view as the wrong place within the right county.
- **Outdoors** the plate fills the frame and the camera moves through it on the scene's
  `camera_strategy`, within a share of the plate's measured limits. The ground moves by the exact
  perspective transform, so it never tears. Wrap a subject that stands on the ground in
  `<PlaceSubject baseY={...}>` with the frame row its base touches, and it rides with its ground.
  Keep type and overlays outside it.
- **Indoors, wide and medium**, the region is outside a window in the back wall. It starts below
  the title band, it is held still and it is bright and soft, the way a camera exposed for the room
  sees a window, behind a light frame. The episode draws its own floor and props in front of it.
- **Indoors, close and detail**, there is no window, only its light: the region is a soft wash
  behind the subject, because a lens that close is focused on the subject and a window pane behind
  a fly makes the fly as tall as the pane. Any view the episode lists in `wash_views` takes the same
  wash at every framing. List a labelled comparison there, things set out on their own ground lines
  with a label over each, since a window's rails and skyline cross exactly that type and those lines.
- **Overhead**, and any view the episode lists in `wall_views` (a diagram or a document, which is
  not in a room), keep plain wall. No more than 40 percent of a film's shots may be wall views.

**An episode never paints a full-frame background.** That one rect hides the whole region, and
the film looks exactly as it did when place was the weakest axis. Paint the floor, the props and
anything the story needs in the room. `scripts/place_check.py --render` renders every shot with the
plate as solid magenta and fails a shot that shows less than its minimum share of region, by
name. Unboxed type over the window stays dark or gets its own panel, as type over any picture does.

The stage also draws a county locator from two seconds in. A small card draws the state's outline,
fills the first scene's county and rings it, on the vetted map-explainer timing (border 2.5
seconds, fill 1.0, label 0.7). It carries no words, because no claim stands behind a board's
county and the narration names the place. Its map is computed by `scripts/county_map.py`.

A run never bakes a plate. A plate is added or changed by editing its scene page and running
`place_bake.py --docket <a TexasAIDocket checkout>`, and the layers and manifest are committed
together. CI fails a scene or a place module edited without a re-bake. Each plate names the engine
record it was drawn with, the Docket commit and the bytes of every engine file, so a plate rebaked
alone with a newer Docket leaves every other plate's record as it was. The bake measures the layers
as the stage loads them, encoded as lossless WebP and read back, and holds each limit to its
measurements: the last step that passed, the next step's failure and every profile end the stage
moves to. CI measures cover and magnification again from the committed layers at every profile end
and requires the bake's numbers exactly. Open each baked plate's `out/place-bake/<plate>/full.png`
at film size before committing it: the bake measures whether the layers move as one world, never
whether the water reads as water.

## Narration and picture use one clock

For new production from October 8th, every spoken clause has a narration-picture-v1 binding in board.narration_picture. Write exact clause text, concrete subject_ids, executable action_id, source claim_ids, scene_id, cue_ids and event_ids before voice production. Cover all words and qualifiers once in their original order. The registered episode declares which views actually implement those subjects and actions. A topic match, caption or label cannot replace a pictured causal step.

Before voice exists, use timing_mode authored with an explicit provisional cue plan for the silent two-treatment comparison. These estimated windows approve only planning. After alignment, board_retime.py replaces them with measured_caption_boundaries from the actual captions and acoustic word stream. Timed capture, preship and delivery require those measured inputs and reject an authored clock.

After acoustic alignment, compile every clause window from complete measured caption boundaries and the matched positional word stream. Use modern_film.compile_narration with the actual captions and words. Derive cut handoffs from silence between clauses. Only framing subdivisions inside the same subject/action may use fractions. Renderer performances consume requireNarration on the film-global clock, and retain completed consequences across cuts. Never stretch speech, scale cue times, or proportionally place a different narrated action inside a scene.

Run scripts/modern_film.py with --board, --captions, --words, --script and --claims before timed capture and preship. The gate rejects missing or duplicated clauses, omitted qualifiers, stale timing, wrong condition identity, incompatible renderer views and gaps in matching picture coverage. These checks establish bindings, not audience understanding. Code, phone and final reviewers inspect the actual subject and performed action for every clause. Return narration_picture_observations bound to the exact film, with ordered clauses containing id, pass, exact start_s/end_s and observed. Preserve a wrong or absent picture as a source/comprehension blocker even if provider metadata says pass.

A current clause must remain understandable with its captions covered. Introduce the spoken subject before its clause begins, perform the narrated change while it is heard, and retain the relevant result through the clause end. Distinguish selection, analysis, test condition, observed result and clinical limit. Generic clinical forms, a repeated test picture under an AI-selection line, or the normal condition under a patient-variant line fail this contract.

# Fresh relevant artwork during every storyboard

Direct owner instruction from October 7th, 2026. From the effective date in
`config/story_art.json`, generate two fresh images before animation and voice. This is a
required production step: a finished hero plus supporting props or a purposeful environment.
Use the built-in ImageGen tool and its skill. Do not silently substitute the old exceptional
Gemini background-plate lane, library boxes or a prior edition's generated artwork.

## Design a useful asset set

After selecting the earned angle, write `story_art` in the actual board, with version
`fresh-story-art-v1` and two `requests`. Each has `id`, `role` (`hero` or `support`), the edition's
`generated/story-art/<date>/<request-id>.png` filename, relevant `scene_ids`, a concrete `purpose`,
the complete generation `prompt`, and an immediate `source_limit`. Plan these images once for
both complete treatments. A supporting atlas can hold several separated relevant props in one
image; its independently movable slices must be measured against the actual output.

Specify recognizable silhouettes, rounded sculpted forms, coherent perspective, layered
materials, motivated key/fill/rim light, readable surface detail and grounded contact. Match the
story's palette and shape language. A film about field work, policy or clinical decisions needs
different objects and a different world. Neither decorative scenery nor a familiar stock
server qualifies. Give every principal on-screen prop a clear story job.

Generate cutouts with genuine transparent alpha when they need to move independently. Preserve
the original alpha and bytes. Use an environment image only when its setting is useful and
clearly generic. Generated art must not impersonate documentary footage, source evidence, a
named real operator, an actual unobserved installation, or measured data. Render exact facts,
labels and captions with native verified text. Show the illustration disclosure.

## Charge, generate, inspect, record

Read the ImageGen skill and announce its first use. Reserve before each actual tool attempt:

```sh
python scripts/story_art.py --board out/dispatch/storyboard.json reserve \
  --state out/dispatch/run_state.json --request <id> --out out/dispatch/art-<id>-charge.json
```

Then invoke built-in ImageGen using that exact request, inspect the returned image at native
size and phone size, and save its original output into the workspace. Record the actual
generation identity from the tool's output filename and its actual creation time, never an
invented provider receipt, token usage or cost:

```sh
python scripts/story_art.py --board out/dispatch/storyboard.json record \
  --source <original-output.png> --request <id> --generation-id <actual-tool-output-id> \
  --generated-at <actual-output-creation-time> --charge out/dispatch/art-<id>-charge.json
python scripts/story_art.py --board out/dispatch/storyboard.json verify
```

All commands use the Dispatch environment wrapper. Add measured image `width` and `height`
and, for an atlas, each named `slices` rectangle `[x,y,width,height]` to the recorded entry.
The record binds exact request, original bytes, edition date and prior charge. A rejected
generation remains charged and retained; archive its board and image before replacing the
current request with a separately named request and asset. Keep exactly two selected assets
in the active plan. Reuse unchanged
assets within this edition's two treatments and mandatory repairs. Resume recorded assets
without buying them again. An unfinished edition can generate its missing or corrected assets
on a later day; its reservation still belongs to that edition's original cumulative ledger.
No image from an earlier edition counts as fresh.

The new normal budget reserves two ImageGen calls, with a cumulative ceiling in run_limits.
Every failed attempt counts. Mandatory art failures use the versioned autonomous completion
policy and exact independent failure evidence to fund the complete remaining path. Optional
asset polish stops at its boundary. The saved primary model, schedule and existing review
count remain unchanged.

`deliver_run.sh` verifies and explicitly stages these exact images, even though the general
generated-asset directory is ignored by Git. The clean release checkout and future review
packets must contain the selected raster bytes. Do not commit unrelated generated files.

## Make the images perform

The active episode consumes `board.story_art` through `StoryArtProvider` and `ArtSprite`, or an
equally explicit reviewed consumer for its story. No hard-coded old image path or vector-box
fallback is allowed. Crop an atlas in the renderer without changing original pixels. Render
these cutouts through Remotion's load-aware `Img` inside the crop viewport. Unmanaged SVG
`image` tags produced missing props at the first frame of a newly mounted shot in the actual
engineering film. The retained cold-shot regression must reject that capture and accept the
loaded picture. Asset download or a good later still does not prove every captured frame.
Animate
actual tasks with setup, contact, reaction and consequence on the global event clock. Change
shot size and viewpoint when the new information earns it. A generated still slowly zoomed
for the whole narration is still a weak film.

The existing builder reports actual image consumers and known limitations. The existing phone
critic and three final scorers inspect visible finish, subject recognition, contact and source
truth on the exact film. Generate attractive art, then prove that it helps this specific story.

# Fresh authored story pictures

The owner selected this Claude substitute on October 9th, 2026. It applies only to a board with
`story_art.version` set to `authored-story-art-v1` and runtime `claude-sonnet-v1`. Older boards
continue to use their original raster ImageGen policy. The finished-art, modern engagement and
independent rendered observations remain unchanged.

Create two original story-specific source groups, hero and support, in
`video-engine/src/modern/episodes/<edition-id>/`. Use source-bound physical actions to choose the
forms. Design recognizable silhouettes, purposeful surface detail, coherent perspective and
lighting, grounded weight and contact, and a performed answer. Use the current regional stage.
Shared primitives can support the work; a renamed old hero or untouched decorative module is not
fresh story artwork. No previous edition's footage or generated art becomes this edition's hero.

The board's `story_art` plan has `version`, `runtime`, `edition_id`, exactly two `requests` and
exactly two recorded `entries`. Each request declares `id`, `role`, source `file`, named `export`,
`scene_ids`, the directed `prompt`, `purpose`, `source_limit` and concrete `action_uses`. An action
use declares `scene_id`, `event_id`, `view`, `action_id` and `subject_ids`. Bind each to the actual
scene event, directed shot and registry narration view. Register the two files in the episode's
`assets` and its `authored_art` rows, each with `role`, `module`, `export` and implemented `views`.
Use those exports in the episode's actual source. Keep the full renderer closure hash-bound.

Reserve the existing builder reboard before authoring either group. That one actual worker can
create both source groups; it is not two external image calls. Do not consume `image_generations`
or invent generation ids, image sizes, PNG source files or image-service charges. Record actual

# Texas AI Dispatch on Claude

Owner directive, October 9th, 2026. This is the Claude host entry point. Read the current
`prompts/dispatch_routine.md` and execute its five phases in full, loading each phase and its
required contracts when entering it. This entry point replaces only the host routing, unavailable
ImageGen service and local workspace bootstrap. Every source, rights, action, modern film, audio,
caption, independent scoring, native rendering and shipment requirement remains in force.

## One outcome

Create a great fresh Texas film and ship it. Continue through the controller's mandatory recovery
until `finish --result shipped` accepts current release evidence, canonical phone playback and a
correctly addressed, read-back unsent Gmail draft. Verify its durable public-safe archive too.
Never send email or post socially. A cloud session marked successful is not shipment evidence.
Never fabricate a review, replace a rejected verdict, discard charges, or loosen an integrity gate.

The owner's October 16th instruction forbids routine permission stops. When an internal tool,
packet, review, storage or controller defect blocks the next command, retain the actual error,
repair its owning code in a clean isolated checkout, run the narrow regression and required CI,
merge the repair, and resume the same edition autonomously. Use standing completion capacity
for mandatory deficits. An internal repair never needs another owner approval. Keep account
funding, credentials, sends and destructive history outside this authority. Notify an external
dependency failure once, retain its executable recovery, and resume on restored access; never
call the run successful or shipped while a required gate is missing.

The owner explicitly requested Sonnet as director and original authored graphics instead of the
built-in image service that Claude does not provide. Apply `config/claude_runtime.json` to newly
planned Claude editions. Do not retrofit this policy into historical or unfinished frozen runs.
Historical October 8th and October 9th films keep their original exact bytes and evidence.

## Wake and safe edition selection

Use a clean current `origin/main` checkout of `Talonsturgill/TexasAIDispatch`, alongside
`Talonsturgill/TexasAIDocket`. Preserve any unrelated work. Read `CLAUDE.md` and the existing
worklog. Cloud worklogs belong in `out/dispatch/WORKLOG.md`; protected settings are edited through
the repository's bootstrap tooling, never by requesting a daily approval.

Run every Dispatch shell command through `bash scripts/run_with_env.sh`. In a worktree explicitly
`cd` into that worktree inside the wrapped shell. Configure the owner's Git identity from
`CLAUDE.md`; never append assistant attribution. Required bindings come from the routine's
existing environment, never source files or printed secrets. Validate voice, full FFmpeg/FFprobe,
fonts, locked dependencies, managed browser, audiovisual provider and the connected Gmail profile
before any paid production work. Install only missing or changed pinned dependencies. Local
workspace housekeeping is used when available. Cloud uses scripts/dispatch_housekeeping.py with
the same protection rules and its actual two checkout paths; never delete active or unrelated work.

The Texas environment must run `scripts/claude_environment_setup.sh` before Claude Code launches.
Setup supplies truthful selected-repository and application-durability context in Claude's user
settings through `claude_environment_context.py`. It preserves all permission rules, defaults,
hooks, model, effort and bindings; project settings do not supply auto-mode context. Retain the
helper's preservation receipt and use `claude auto-mode config` to verify the effective context
on a fresh host. Keep existing credential and no-send boundaries.
The saved prelaunch setup includes this command before Claude starts:

```sh
bash scripts/run_with_env.sh python3 scripts/claude_environment_context.py --workspace /home/user --apply
```

The versioned setup provisions pinned tools and registers the workspace capture router once,
before auto mode begins. Do not attempt mid-session registration or repeat a classifier-denied
installation. Preserve the denied command evidence and use a fresh supported routine launch
after the environment setup is corrected. Setup success does not prove a loaded hook; retain
the actual harmless probe denial before production capture.

Cloud environment provisioning is cached. Editing GitHub main does not rerun its setup script.
The October 19 setup revision installs `claude_session_start.py` as a primary-workspace
SessionStart hook before launch. Each actual startup or resume refreshes only the clean owned
tools checkout from the existing origin main and records `.claude/dispatch-session-start.json`.
Read that receipt and compare its current source bindings before production. The capture and
checkpoint codec guards remain unchanged. A stale cache is an internal startup defect, never a
reason to stop for owner permission. Repair the versioned setup, save its exact current text in
the existing Texas environment to rebuild the cached setup, and use a fresh supported launch.
Do not edit permissions, disable the codec check or register a hook inside an active host.
The environment setup and SessionStart lifecycle are documented at
https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cloud-environments#environment-caching .

In a fresh Linux cloud checkout run the idempotent setup, then re-enter the wrapper so its
external cache is active. The first command installs only absent or changed pinned tools;
the second actually proves voice/alignment and render access before reservations:

```sh
bash scripts/run_with_env.sh python3 scripts/cloud_bootstrap.py --bind-only
bash scripts/run_with_env.sh python scripts/cloud_bootstrap.py
bash scripts/run_with_env.sh python scripts/claude_contract_check.py
```

Resolve the actual sibling checkout paths and their shared workspace parent. Run the versioned
housekeeping helper at startup and after the verified shipped archive:

```sh
bash scripts/run_with_env.sh python scripts/dispatch_housekeeping.py --workspace <shared-parent> --dispatch-repo <actual-dispatch-checkout> --docket-repo <actual-docket-checkout> --apply --fetch --summary
```

Before every native render, calculate scripts/native_headroom.py on the current board, then repeat
that housekeeping command with --require-headroom --min-free-gib set to its required_free_gib.
Retain at least two completed packages. Missing process inspection or unverifiable archives never
authorize cleanup; recover the actual capacity condition through the controller.

Read knowledge/craft/AUTHORED_STORY_ART.md and config/authored_story_art.json during the
picture phase. Use its actual record, verify and stage commands. There is no ImageGen call
in this lane and no fabricated image-generation charge.

Run `run_controller.py pending` and resume the oldest unfinished production before making a new
edition. A cloud container is reclaimed, so `pending` alone sees only worktrees that still exist.
Also run `python scripts/claude_checkpoint.py discover`. Select the OLDEST unfinished edition by its run identity and creation time
(`claude_checkpoint.py discover --oldest-unfinished`, never the first row of the newest-save-first list)
and resume its existing ledger. It is restored
with `python scripts/claude_checkpoint.py restore --run-id <id> --origin-workspace <shared-parent>`.
The recorded original root preserves absolute paths inside unchanged hash-bound historical events;
the fresh scheduled October 18 recovery proved this route after a different-root restore failed.
The helper accepts only an empty real directory inside the selected shared workspace and never
removes an occupied destination. Inspect an occupied original checkout for the same active edition,
its current ledger and owner before resuming it; preserve unrelated work. Retain any failed restore
and its audit. Do not rewrite historical grant text or hashes to fit a new path. That
creates an isolated checkout of the recorded source commit (the complete committed renderer, art and
public closure), overlays the verified scratch outputs and uncommitted source, and rebuilds the same
ledger, frozen envelope, charges, failed reviews and paid outputs with its paths moved. It never
touches another checkout or an existing ledger, has no force option, and refuses a finished edition.
Bind its exact lockfile dependencies from the preinstalled environment using the current
`scripts/cloud_bootstrap.py --bind-only --repo <restored-checkout>` helper, then resume.
Immediately after restore, before any paid worker reservation, run that binding through the
current-main wrapper, then explicitly cd into the restored checkout inside the wrapped shell
and run its `python scripts/env_check.py --require-voice`. Retain both exit codes. The wake
check on the primary checkout is not a runtime check on the restored checkout. A missing
Python import, Node module, browser or pinned alignment tool must be repaired from the
preinstalled cache before a paid builder or render. Never use a scratch tsconfig or scratch
source copy as a substitute for the production checkout's actual typecheck. Run the actual
`cd video-engine && npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` before accepting a builder hand-back.
Never initialise a second
ledger for an edition that has a checkpoint.

For a new edition with no pending ledger or checkpoint, keep the primary bootstrap checkout clean.
Create its production worktree at `<shared-parent>/dispatch-editions/<run-id>/TexasAIDispatch`
from current `origin/main`, with the real Docket sibling required below. Use that owned checkout
for the whole edition and record its actual paths. Its recorded origin is then empty on a fresh
cloud host. Inspect an occupied edition directory and resume its owner instead of creating a
duplicate. Keep the existing remote checkpoint concurrency checks before every charged dispatch;
a stale writer must not buy another attempt or overwrite newer history.

Before authorizing capture in a restored or nested worktree, establish a real clean Docket
checkout at `<dispatch-checkout-parent>/TexasAIDocket`, starting at current origin/main. An owned
isolated clone or a suitable registered worktree satisfies this requirement.
The capture helper runs housekeeping against that sibling and their shared parent. A symlink to
the primary Docket checkout fails the bounded-workspace check. Preserve the primary checkout and
all unrelated or dirty work; use this owned sibling for the narrow Dispatch feed release. Retain
any failed path inspection and its charged reservation, then verify the normal housekeeping gate.

Derive today's calendar date in the schedule timezone from config/claude_runtime.json;
the cloud host's UTC date does not select an Eastern edition. A terminal shipped run is immutable.
The first owner-authorized migration test uses a
fresh current story and an intentional distinct run identity `<today>-claude-pilot`, including its
own branch, scratch, permanent media, feed identity, draft and archive. The board's calendar date
is still today. Run this migration pilot only if no prior Claude pilot has accepted `shipped`
status and a verified durable archive in `runs/`. Resume an unfinished pilot instead of creating
another. After that one pilot is archived, every scheduled invocation uses normal daily production.
Normal scheduled production uses today's date. If today's scheduled film is
already shipped, verify that shipment and do not manufacture another ordinary edition.

## Durable checkpoints and effective effort

`out/` is gitignored and dies with the container. For an edition marked by
`out/dispatch/claude-host.json`, every controller ledger write is mirrored to
`claude/checkpoint/<run-id>` before the writer returns, so each reservation is durable before its
paid call is dispatched. After each paid call returns and its output is on disk, the same mirror
runs again through the next ledger write, and `python scripts/claude_checkpoint.py save --note <what>`
covers outputs written without one. Prefer `claude_checkpoint.py guard --note <what> -- <paid command>`,
which makes state durable, runs the command and makes its outputs durable, and exits 75 when it can't.
A checkpoint that cannot be made after storage and transport recovery writes
`out/dispatch/checkpoint-unbacked.json`, raises, and blocks every new reservation until
`claude_checkpoint.py recover` succeeds. Never continue paid work on an unbacked ledger.
The controller also verifies the current snapshot before it changes any reservation counter.
If a newer writer already advanced the remote edition, this stale invocation preserves its
unchanged ledger and failed evidence without buying another attempt. Keep the newer checkpoint
authoritative, preserve both hosts, and resume that edition through the existing restoration and
continuation workflow. Never overwrite newer history or repeat the paid command from the stale host.

The checkpoint keeps the sanitized ledger, authored source, claims, board, voice takes, alignment,
review responses, failed images and every receipt. It skips only known rebuildable directories
(frames, tmp, cache). It leaves out Gmail, routing and credential material by any path component or
data structure, redacts shipped Gmail identifiers and local paths from the ledger, refuses to save when
a credential value appears, and refuses any save that would lower usage, limits or increments, change the
frozen envelope or alter the earlier event history. A file too large to retain fails the save visibly.
From the October 17 edition, the cinema producer creates its duplicate render cache under
`out/dispatch/tmp/cinema-render-cache`. Canonical proof images, hero, provenance and every failed
proof remain under `cinema/` and are retained. Earlier editions keep their original cache path.
After `finish --result shipped` and the metadata archive, save once more so the checkpoint reads finished.

Immediately after selecting or restoring the production ledger, arm its preinstalled completion
guard through the current checkout. Resolve the actual registered primary workspace, then run:

```sh
bash scripts/run_with_env.sh python scripts/routine_continuation.py --workspace <registered-primary-workspace> --arm out/dispatch/run_state.json
```

For cloud production the helper verifies the installed Stop registration and settings, resolves
an ancestor primary workspace when given a nested edition parent, and prints the exact watched
marker. A nested checkout parent is not automatically the hook's workspace. Verify that printed
marker matches the installed registration. Missing or changed registration refuses arming rather
than reporting success in an unwatched folder.

Repeat this after a later restoration too. If the earlier armed path no longer exists, the
helper can retarget the same edition only after verifying the immutable checkpoint ledger,
unchanged frozen envelope and complete cumulative event history. It retains a rebind audit.
A live earlier ledger or another edition stays protected. Do not hand-edit the marker or
re-register hooks to get around a refused rebind.

The prelaunch Stop hook sends an early final response back to this same ledger. It approves no
tool, changes no permissions and adds no capacity. It remains inactive for ordinary coding and
leaf agents. A repeated Stop with a running task reported by the host waits twenty seconds,
then rechecks the same shipment closure before returning feedback. This limits idle status
chatter; it never treats a background task as completion. Collect required task results through
the actual task tools, repair internal failures
through the versioned routes, and continue until accepted shipment, the matching public archive
on fetched origin/main, and the final shipped checkpoint exist. Do not re-register hooks in a
running host. A supported fresh environment can prove the actual event with
`routine_continuation.py --workspace <registered-primary-workspace> --probe` before any production is armed;
that one-shot nonproduction probe creates no ledger and cannot replace an armed production run.

At wake also record `python scripts/claude_contract_check.py --effective out/dispatch/effective-effort.json`.
It reads the root session's host effort, any `CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL` override, and each leaf's
frontmatter. Fail on a mismatch; never set a global effort override.

## Claude-native worker routing

The director is `claude-sonnet-5-5` at medium effort. Read the exact role map from
`config/claude_runtime.json`; do not use Codex `spawn_args` in Claude's Agent tool. Use the existing
role roster, adding only the named `scene-builder` leaf definition for the existing builder task.
Pin exact model ids and supported effort in versioned agent frontmatter and project settings.
The owner refined the route on October 9th: scene-builder, storyboard-critic and validator use
Opus 5.5 at high effort. These calls own the authored picture, its independent critique and source
truth. Research and voice direction remain Haiku high; three separate final scorers remain
Sonnet medium. The director stays Sonnet medium. Measure rework and quality before claiming that
the stronger creative workers reduced total run cost.
Spawn `scene-builder` for the existing reserved two-treatment builder assignment, using
`.claude/agents/scene-builder.md` and `prompts/roles/scene-builder.md`. Reuse it for corrections.
Do not globally force `CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL` to medium, because that overrides the leaf's high
effort. Detect and report any inherited override and resolve it before worker execution.

Give each worker a compact current packet with actual input paths and SHA256 bindings, the
relevant phase, full current guide text and hashes, role brief and exact rubric. Isolate its
conversation. Every assignment says to do the work itself and launch no additional agents.
Reserve its actual controller resource before starting. Reuse the builder and critic for bounded
follow-ups, consolidate linked defects and keep one render owner. Three final scorer responses
remain distinct identities and an atomic charged panel on the same finished film. The director
cannot count self-review as independence. Provider recovery is used only after actual observed
host unavailability, under the existing recovery policy.

While a background worker owns required work, use the host's supported task-status and output
tools to wait for that exact task and collect its full handback. Do not end the response merely
to say that you are yielding or waiting; continue the next owned production step when its
result arrives. Confirm the task is actually running before waiting, and explicitly resume a
completed worker when assigning new charged content work. Keep one active owner and never
dispatch a duplicate because a response is slow. An unfinished controller is still active
production even when the cloud UI marks an assistant response successful.

If the task-status tool returns immediately while the worker is still running, use one
twenty-second Bash wait through scripts/run_with_env.sh with the explicit worktree cd inside
the wrapped shell, then check that same task again. Keep these as tool calls in the active
turn, without a final waiting response between them. Do not use a long shell loop or interrupt
the worker to stop idle polling. A read-only status update never requires a new content call.

## Fresh authored picture lane

Follow Alaska's strongest production methods in `Talonsturgill/alaska-ai-weekly`: recognizable
story-specific cast and equipment, motivated depth, physical actions and consequences, sound
connected to the picture, varied useful framing, early earned changes and a performed ending.
Inspect the current source and shipped film; never copy Alaska's history, dedupe ledger, footage,
place or character defaults. Texas place, source-bound actions and house voice remain Texas.

Create exactly two fresh relevant authored asset groups, hero and support, shared by exactly two
complete visual treatments. Build finished recognizable forms with coherent perspective, regional
palette, motivated lighting, surface detail and believable contact. Original SVG, React/CSS-depth
and Three.js through the current Remotion engine are allowed. Do not imitate ImageGen metadata or
claim an external generation happened. Record actual creation time, exact source module bytes,
edition identity, source claim hashes, declared exports and each performed on-screen use. Bind the
complete renderer dependency closure. Changed shared parts do not become fresh artwork by renaming
them. A reused prior-edition hero, unused decorative asset, generic boxes, slideshow or legacy
whole-episode rescue fails the new lane.

Implement the authored lane as a dated, explicit Claude opt-in, retaining the original raster
ImageGen policy and all historical tests. Its mechanical gate must reject missing/stale modules,
unrelated sources, absent current action use, repeated old asset identities and unresolved imports.
The existing independent phone, native hero and exact-film reviews judge the actual pixels under
all seven modern observations. Mechanically correct bindings do not establish visual quality.
Retain the active `directed-film-v2` route and complete source/event/clause-bound shot timeline.

Prove both complete silent phone treatments before voice, then measured timed phone, native hero
with sound, final cut, all audiovisual lenses, panel and delivery. Before native renders calculate

Recover only eligible storage if the actual plan lacks room. Never lower native 1080x1920 capture,
PNG, CRF16 or mandatory reviews. Reserve every actual attempt before execution. Fund the complete
remaining review and delivery path before correcting a failed cut. Keep the frozen envelope,
cumulative usage, individual authorized increments and exact failure evidence.

For an independently rejected mandatory code defect before a film exists, use the merged
code-evidence amendment in knowledge/craft/AUTONOMOUS_COMPLETION.md. Keep the original failed
report and before-files. Bind a new plan with scripts/autonomous_completion.py
--prepare-code-plan <original-plan> --claims <claims> --output <new-plan>, then run the controller's
production-budget and completion-capacity on that new plan before beginning its correction.
This preserves the original frozen adoption and adds only exact conservative deficits.
Code evidence cannot approve pixels or replace either complete phone treatment or final reviews.
Do not request a daily decision at the internal critic ceiling.

After an independent passing code review, stop optional editing. If contract failures consumed
the funded reviews, use the actual new independent passing report in a finish-current plan with

and completion-capacity on that new finish plan, retaining every prior failure, grant and charge.

## Efficiency and actual usage

finish-current plan. Normal completion-capacity may grant exactly one separately recorded

Keep phase loading, compact assignments, exact-byte audiovisual caching including failures, and

dependent production commands into one exit-code-checked job with retained logs and a compact
summary, stopping at the first mandatory failure. Use exact job handles and completion markers;
avoid repeated full-context polling. Use supported nonblocking worker status or waits of at most
60 seconds; do not block steering or completed handbacks with long Bash sleep loops. Reuse the
same worker for output-format corrections with exact gate errors. Give it the current report
contract and computed bindings before execution; use bounded gate-function excerpts for missing

An October 18 anonymous curl status poll was classifier-denied without an explanation; the
ordinary GitHub connector completed the read. Retain such a denial and use that natural read

of the wait shell's own command. Retain completed check receipts and stop only a confirmed

through scripts/run_with_env.sh. Follow AUTONOMOUS_COMPLETION.md for the separate pinned modern

Measure actual Claude input, cache creation/read and output tokens by phase and worker, external

PR, a preview, a passing panel or an uploaded file. Complete the original five-phase master through

## Canonical phone playback on the cloud host

### Complete silent phone evidence before voice

Image delivery is load-aware for every Claude phone and final image-only reviewer. The host
has actually stripped image results from large Read batches. A complete index on disk does
not prove that the model received its pages. The current packet pins one image Read per model
step, no parallel image Reads, and concrete per-page notes before the next Read. Read full
